#15887. Prediction: Dec. 9 Will Mark a Turning Point for the S&P 500

Prediction: Dec. 9 Will Mark a Turning Point for the S&P 500

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (544 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that suddenly, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.04%) doesn't look so hot anymore.
  • Meanwhile, the controversy surrounding Nvidia and its former CEO, Jensen Huang, has raised further concerns in the tech sector and broader markets.
  • In a recent development, however, the massive date for investors to mark on their calendars is undoubtedly Dec.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that suddenly, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.04%) doesn't look so hot anymore. It has declined by 3% over the past month as bearishness in the tech sector has been weighing on the broader markets. Plus, with interest rates on the rise and questionable economic conditions, investors have been more eager of late to sell stocks, especially highly valued ones.

Meanwhile, the controversy surrounding Nvidia and its former CEO, Jensen Huang, has raised further concerns in the tech sector and broader markets.

In a recent development, however, the massive date for investors to mark on their calendars is undoubtedly Dec. 9. That's the day the Fed makes its next interest-rate decision, and it could be a big one. Here's why I predict it'll be a turning point for the S&P 500.

In a recent development, the likelihood of another rate hike next month is all but certain. It's just a matter of how significant an increase it may be. According to CME Group's FedWatch tool, there is more than a 94% probability that interest rates will rise by 25 basis points, bringing the target range to 4.00% to 4.25%. The probability of rates remaining unchanged is zero, while the probability of a half-point rate hike is just under 6%.

But depending on the economic data that comes out between now and then, things could change. Christopher Waller, who is a member of the Federal Reserve's board of governors, has said he supports a 50-basis-point hike, particularly if consumer price data continue to paint a troubling picture. And last week's inflation report came in higher than expected, confirming Waller's concerns.

Even if a half-point hike doesn't happen, however, simply an increase in interest rates by 25 basis points could be enough to weigh on the markets, as it may effectively be confirmation that inflation isn't under control, and that given the Fed's serious stance on it, even more rate hikes could be on the horizon in 2027.

The S&P 500 has been falling, and its gains for the year are now around 8%, but the more concerning the outlook for the stock market, the more likely the index is to come down in the final weeks of the year.

I believe Dec. 9 will be a key turning point for the market, as news of another rate hike will trigger even greater selling, potentially leading the S&P 500 into a correction and possibly even a bear market before the year is over. It's thus more important than ever for investors to consider looking at safe investments to put into their portfolios.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Michael Burry gained popular fame after author Michael Lewis chronicled his prescient shorting of the mortgage market ahead of the subprime mortgage crisis in his book The Substantial Short, which later was made into a movie of the same name.
    • In a recent development, burry made hundreds of millions for himself and his investors thanks to that bet.
    • According to recent reports, michael Burry.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Michael Burry gained popular fame after author Michael Lewis chronicled his prescient shorting of the mortgage market ahead of the subprime mortgage crisis in his book The Substantial Short, which later was made into a movie of the same name.

    In a recent development, burry made hundreds of millions for himself and his investors thanks to that bet. Some years after closing the hedge fund he ran during the 2000s, he opened a fresh one called Scion Asset Management, which he closed down in 2025.

    According to recent reports, michael Burry. Image source: Getty Images.

    Now, he’s only investing his own money, so he's no longer required to report his positions quarterly to the Securities and Exchange Commission. But he still offers detailed trade info and his personal musings through his Substack and on X. He has been outspoken against the artificial intelligence (AI) trade, and he has specifically cited Nvidia (NVDA -0.63%) many times, likening how it operates to the mafia.

    He has held a short position in Nvidia for some time, and with that stock down sharply since peaking in early October, he could be making another fortune.

    Burry has been critical of Nvidia's circular financing deals for years.

    The chipmaker's take is that there are many small companies that don't have the money to buy its top-of-the-line graphics processing units (GPUs), the foundational hardware for AI development, so it provides them with financing so that they can have a place at the table. It predominantly does this in two ways: It acts as a backstop for third-party financing, and it invests in some clients, providing money in exchange for equity stakes in those smaller companies. The most well-known of these arrangements is probably with CoreWeave (CRWV +0.06%), in which Nvidia has invested more than $2 billion.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:52 AM ET 11/17/26.

    Burry noted that the U.S. Department of Justice was already investigating Nvidia for several actions, including its acquisition of AI development platform Hugging Face. He has likened Nvidia's business model to a "protection racket," alleging that it forced clients to buy its products and abused its dominant position in the AI chip space.

    Burry first disclosed a short position in Nvidia through public filings for Scion Asset Management last year, just before he shut the hedge fund down. Since then, he has bought put options on Nvidia due in December, but closed out that position in September. According to his Substack, he still has a short position in Nvidia. In the meantime, he has turned to shorting other AI stocks and exchange-traded funds.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia stock is down 32% since it hit a high on Oct. 6, and it's very possible that Burry is making a fortune right now.

    The lesson for investors is to consider all risks before deciding on a position, or the size of a position, even if it's in a popular stock. There’s no indication that Burry was previously aware of the affairs that ultimately brought down Huang, but he did call out unusual activity that may end up having an even harsher impact on the organization and its stock.

    Anthropic's Quarterly Revenue Jumped 47% to $17 Billion Ahead of Its IPO

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (601 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic is set to price its IPO Wednesday and begin trading Thursday.
    • The highly anticipated IPO isn't just an vital moment for the organization and its shareholders -- it also represents a test of the health of the broader artificial intelligence (AI) trade.
    • It has been revealed that AI stocks have been volatile recently due to macroeconomic dynamics, funding concerns, and news related to the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang -- and the market's appetite for Anthropic's IPO could provide a valuable indicator of what investors can expect in valuation moves within the category.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic is set to price its IPO Wednesday and begin trading Thursday. The stage is set for what could be one of this year's most notable stock market events.

    The highly anticipated IPO isn't just an vital moment for the organization and its shareholders -- it also represents a test of the health of the broader artificial intelligence (AI) trade.

    It has been revealed that AI stocks have been volatile recently due to macroeconomic dynamics, funding concerns, and news related to the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang -- and the market's appetite for Anthropic's IPO could provide a valuable indicator of what investors can expect in valuation moves within the category. While it's impossible to say with certainty exactly where AI stocks will go in the near term, it's clear that there is strong appetite for Anthropic's technologies and services.

    According to recent reports, in the lead-up to its IPO, Anthropic filed an amended S-1 form with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) that added a breakdown of its business performance to supplement its previously disclosed results across the first half of the year. Strikingly, Anthropic's revenue rose from $11.6 billion in the second quarter to roughly $17 billion in the third quarter -- representing approximately 47% sequential growth.

    Sources indicate that the Q3 revenue numbers show rapid scaling for service sales from the tech giant's Claude software suite. For context, the company recorded roughly $16.3 billion in revenue across this year's first two quarters. Sales in the third quarter alone exceeded the combined revenue from the first and second quarters.

    The performance suggests that demand for the tech giant's tech continues to surge -- and that Anthropic is pulling monetization levers that are driving greater spending from its clients. Along those lines, the company's most recent enhancement stated that the artificial intelligence business now had more than 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in revenue over the past 12 months.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:55 AM ET 11/17/26.

    Industry observers note that with the rapid scaling of Anthropic's Claude models, there are clear winners in the artificial intelligence hardware and services space. The most obvious and direct example is Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.78%), which has a massive contract to provide compute to the frontier AI model leader. According to Anthropic's S-1 filing, the firm has a deal in place to purchase up to $120.5 billion in compute from SpaceX through 2029. Either side can cancel on 90 days' notice after early 2027, but it's a substantial agreement.

    It has been revealed that leading hardware providers that source the key components that power SpaceX's compute and other data centers are also poised to win business as Anthropic scales. These companies include Nvidia, Micron, and Broadcom. So while Anthropic's IPO will likely have important near-term implications for valuations in the AI space, the extent of the manufacturer's long-term scaling will ultimately be far more important for buy-and-hold investors.

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (787 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Apple Is Now the World’s Largest Manufacturer. Time to Buy the Stock?

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (787 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia (NVDA -0.18%) was formerly the world's largest tech giant by a fairly wide margin.
    • Industry observers note that that's a monster lead, but has Apple reached a ceiling, or is there more room to run?
    • When you look at the companies that are deeply involved in artificial intelligence (AI), Apple is about the only tech giant that's absent from the list.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia (NVDA -0.18%) was formerly the world's largest tech giant by a fairly wide margin. However, that lead is now gone thanks to the market’s reaction to news of its CEO resigning, and Apple (AAPL +0.70%) is firmly in the lead. As of the time of writing, Apple's market capitalization sits at about $5.2 trillion, while Nvidia's is at $4 trillion.

    Industry observers note that that's a monster lead, but has Apple reached a ceiling, or is there more room to run? I think there are a few things that investors need to watch out for with Apple, as the future doesn't look very promising.

    When you look at the companies that are deeply involved in artificial intelligence (AI), Apple is about the only tech giant that's absent from the list. Nearly every company above a $1 trillion market value is spending big on AI or is a key component provider.

    While Apple has integrated some AI feature sets into its products and upgraded its Siri assistant, all of those technologies are using someone else's AI model. Apple realized that just using someone else's product and deploying it in its software was a far more cost-effective option, and that the market has loved that.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:58 AM ET 11/17/26.

    Instead of Apple spending hundreds of billions of dollars on an extensive data center network, Apple has kept its spending modest and continued to repurchase shares at an aggressive rate. As of now, this looks like the right choice, as all of the deep AI investments some of Apple's peers are making haven't paid off.

    As a result of not going all-in on AI, the stock has become a safe haven for investors who don't want as much exposure to AI. This has caused a lot of investors to buy up the stock, which has inflated its valuation.

    AAPL PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

    Apple is now one of the more expensive stocks on the market, trading at 38 times forward earnings. For reference, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.04%) trades at some one-time gain on investments is skewing net profits and is trading at about 19 times forward earnings. That's a major mismatch, but is Apple's stock worth the premium from a business standpoint? I don't think so.

    While Apple's substantial tech peers are spending big on AI data centers and haven't completely paid for themselves yet, the reality is that these companies are still growing far faster than Apple. Of the five largest companies in the world, Apple is growing the slowest (Nvidia is excluded because its growth rate was over 100% last quarter).

    AAPL Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts.

    It has been revealed that while Apple's growth rate is similar to Amazon's, Amazon's business is also shifting to a heavier reliance on cloud computing, which has better margins. When you look at how swiftly operating profits are growing (net profits are being skewed by some one-time gain on investments), this argument goes away.

    AAPL Operating Income (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts.

    It has been revealed that the reality is that Apple is growing far slower than its peers yet trades for a substantial premium over them. That is an odd mismatch, and it's something that likely won't last forever. Apple is also facing its own challenges, such as the rising cost of components because the AI build-out is consuming a large amount of production capacity at chip companies.

    At the end of the day, Apple is a very dominant company with a very disciplined approach to what it spends money on and how much stock it buys back. This discipline has gotten it to the status of the world's largest company and is unlikely to change anytime soon.

    However, the stock has gotten so expensive that buybacks are less effective. This could dampen future returns on the stock, and while Apple may not crash, I think investors are at serious risk of underperformance over the next few years. As a result, I think there are far better stocks to buy now.

    Top Wall Street analysts prefer these 3 dividend stocks for stable income

    📅 11 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (940 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, uncertainty in the Middle East, elevated Treasury yields and fears about an AI bubble continue to keep global markets on edge.
    • According to recent reports, however, the vast universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, uncertainty in the Middle East, elevated Treasury yields and fears about an AI bubble continue to keep global markets on edge. Given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking stable income can consider enhancing their portfolios by adding dividend-paying stocks.

    According to recent reports, however, the vast universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Tracking the ratings of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as their recommendations are backed by in-depth research.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Industry observers note that chord Energy is an independent exploration and production manufacturer with long-lived assets primarily in the Williston Basin. With a quarterly base dividend of $1.30 per share, CHRD offers a dividend yield of 3.67%.

    Recent findings suggest that in a research note on third-quarter expectations, RBC Capital analyst Scott Hanold reiterated a buy rating on CHRD stock with a price target of $175. "We model production near the top of guidance and continue to see strong performance from new wells and base production," stated Hanold.

    According to recent reports, specifically, the five-star analyst expects Q3 2026 production at 283 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, or Mboe/d, in line with the Street's consensus and near the high end of the 278 to 284 Mboe/d guidance. Hanold said his Q3 2026 earnings per share estimate increased to $5.29 due to lower non-cash depreciation, depletion and amortization.

    Sources indicate that meanwhile, cash flow per share estimate moved lower to $13.59 to reflect Hanold's upgrade based on the current backdrop and commodity mark-to-market. He expects Chord Energy to report capital spending of $375 million for Q3 2026, slightly above the Street's estimate of $369 million.

    Overall, Hanold remains bullish on CHRD, given its best-in-class balance sheet. He expects a free cash flow payout of 80% in the third quarter, with the possibility of an upside. Hanold expects investors to focus on management commentary on 2027 capital plans, Williston M&A opportunities, and long-term performance of 4-mile wells.

    Recent findings suggest that hanold ranks No. 310 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 14.9%. See Chord Energy KPIs on TipRanks.

    Williams, an energy infrastructure organization that delivers natural gas, is the next dividend pick. The company recently completed the $5.5 billion acquisition of Momentum Midstream, which will expand its natural gas infrastructure in the Haynesville to meet growing Gulf Coast LNG, power and industrial demand. At a quarterly dividend of $0.5250 per share, Williams offers a yield of 2.89%.

    Sources indicate that in her latest research note, RBC Capital analyst Elvira Scotto reiterated a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $87. Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, the analyst said that she expects WMB to announce strong quarterly performance.

    According to recent reports, scotto raised her estimates to reflect insights from the quarterly catch-up call, the completion of the Momentum Midstream acquisition, and mark-to-market quarter-to-date commodity prices. She expects WMB to report Q3 2026 adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $2,036 million, which is modestly above the Street's consensus estimate.

    Furthermore, Scotto expects Williams' Transmission, Power & Gulf segment to increase quarter-over-quarter, driven by the startup of the Socrates power project and favorable natural gas liquids, or NGL, margins.

    Scotto noted that WMB stock has underperformed due to backlash related to data centers and investor anticipation of another Power Innovation project. She expects the firm to announce at least one more project before the end of this year, potentially with a new customer and a contract duration of 15 to 20 years, which would be a positive catalyst for the stock.

    In a recent development, scotto ranks No. 175 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been profitable 67% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.2%. See Williams Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Recent findings suggest that EOG Resources, a crude oil and natural gas exploration and production organization, will hold its third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 6. At a quarterly dividend of $1.02 per share, EOG offers a dividend yield of 2.75%.

    Recent findings suggest that heading into Q3 earnings, Jefferies analyst Lloyd Byrne reiterated a buy rating on EOG Resources stock and increased his price target to $185 from $175. The analyst expects the manufacturer's Q3 cash flow per share to exceed the Street's consensus by 13%, driven by better-than-expected production.

    Byrne expects crude oil production, excluding the UAE, to reach 551 Mboe/d, which is at the high end of guidance (546-551 Mboe/d) and above the Street's projection of 548 Mboe/d, driven by continued growth in the Utica.

    Furthermore, Byrne expects cash operating expenses to come in at $10.27 per barrel of oil equivalent, below the midpoint of guidance of $10.05 to $11.35, helped by lower lease operating expenses. Overall, the analyst expects EOG to deliver free cash flow of $2.65 billion, supporting another quarter of buybacks near the minimum 70% shareholder return threshold and implying about $1.5 billion in share repurchases.

    "As a first indication of the '27 initiative, we expect EOG will message another year of mid-single-digit (~3.5%) growth on a flat capital budget (~$6.55bn), which is above the Street modeling 1% oil growth at $6.6bn," said Byrne.

    Byrne ranks No. 303 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 18.5%. See EOG Resources Statistics on TipRanks.

    #15862. Breaking: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

    📅 05 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2174 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

    📅 05 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2174 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.
    • Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.
    • There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

    Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

    There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

    Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

    Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

    Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

    Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

    Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

    They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

    In a recent development, even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

    In a recent development, juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

    Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

    Industry observers note that chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

    Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

    Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

    Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

    Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

    Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

    Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

    The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

    More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

    Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

    Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

    Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

    Recent findings suggest that chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

    This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

    Industry observers note that palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

    Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

    Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

    For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

    Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

    There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

    Recent findings suggest that far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

    Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

    Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

    Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

    Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

    In a recent development, play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

    Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

    Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

    Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

    It has been revealed that chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

    Recent findings suggest that quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

    In a recent development, welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

    Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

    Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

    Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

    Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

    Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

    Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik.

    Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David.

    Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”.

    Sources indicate that how long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

    Sources indicate that looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

    Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck.

    Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap.

    The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

    Sources indicate that they have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

    Another upcoming arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

    It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

    In a recent development, alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

    Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the growth potential of these 3 stocks

    📅 18 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (942 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.
    • Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

    Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Recent findings suggest that health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The tech giant also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround strategy.

    In a recent development, following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

    The five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the firm's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

    It has been revealed that furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the manufacturer's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

    Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

    Sources indicate that wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

    Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

    Specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active consumers in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    In a recent development, "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently launched Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the company's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

    Morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

    It has been revealed that next is semiconductor manufacturer Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

    After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

    It has been revealed that the five-star analyst said that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

    In a recent development, while XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the manufacturer raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

    Svanberg said that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

    In a recent development, svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Lions' Aidan Hutchinson confirmed to have torn ACL, ending his 2026 season

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (494 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that fears that Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL in his right knee were confirmed after additional exams, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero.
    • On Tuesday, Lions head coach Dan Campbell confirmed that injury, saying "it stinks" and that Hutchinson will come out of it better on the other side.
    • Hutchinson injured his knee on the Lions' first defensive series versus the New England Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that fears that Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL in his right knee were confirmed after additional exams, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero. Though tests reportedly revealed no other significant damage to Hutchinson's knee, he is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season with the injury.

    On Tuesday, Lions head coach Dan Campbell confirmed that injury, saying "it stinks" and that Hutchinson will come out of it better on the other side.

    Hutchinson injured his knee on the Lions' first defensive series versus the New England Patriots on Sunday in Munich. After sacking New England's Drake Maye, Detroit's fifth-year star jumped in celebration and landed awkwardly on his right leg. Hutchinson immediately went to the turf. As teammates and players approached, he gestured to the front of his right knee.

    Campbell added Tuesday that he will not speak with Hutchinson about celebrating plays. Campbell said he didn't want to take emotion out of the game.

    Hutchinson reportedly underwent an MRI after Detroit's 35-10 win that highlighted a torn ACL. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said the defensive end would undergo further testing when the team returned to the U.S. before making an official announcement.

    According to recent reports, "We'll know more when we get back in the States," head coach Dan Campbell noted postgame, via the Detroit News' Nolan Bianchi. "Anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is, he's a captain of ours, that doesn't make things easy.".

    Meanwhile, a fan captured video of Hutchinson in a wheelchair at the airport prior to the Lions traveling back to Michigan on Sunday.

    Maye sustained an injury to his ankle on the same play and the Patriots fear the QB may have suffered a fracture that would end his season. The third-year star stayed in Germany for additional testing that could determine if he needs surgery, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed during a radio interview Monday.

    In nine games this season, Hutchinson recorded 6 sacks and 24 total tackles in addition to 1 pass defended and 1 forced fumble.

    Hutchinson's torn ACL is the second serious, season-ending injury that he has sustained during his NFL career. During the 2024 season, he suffered a broken fibula and tibia in his left leg during a Week 6 win over the Dallas Cowboys. Hutchinson recovered to play in all 17 games last year, compiling 14.5 sacks.

    It has been revealed that the Lions' 2022 first-round draft pick (No. 2 overall) out of Michigan, Hutchinson has been named to two Pro Bowls and earned second-team All-Pro honors during his career. He's compiled 49 sacks in 65 games with 200 tackles and 5 interceptions.

    Recent findings suggest that last year, Hutchinson signed a four-year, $180 million contract extension (including $141 million in guaranteed money). That extension kicks in next season following the fifth-year option the Lions picked up this year.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Leading prediction market platform Kalshi will offer stock trading within the next few months, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC.
    • Recent findings suggest that the platform's move to offer equity trading is the boldest so far in its ongoing push into traditional financial markets and comes amid an escalating fight by states and lawmakers against its sports trading business.
    • In September, the platform introduced perpetual futures tied to precious metals such as gold and silver after it had originally filed in July to offer beyond prediction market event contracts with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal regulator overseeing derivatives contracts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Leading prediction market platform Kalshi will offer stock trading within the next few months, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC.

    Recent findings suggest that the platform's move to offer equity trading is the boldest so far in its ongoing push into traditional financial markets and comes amid an escalating fight by states and lawmakers against its sports trading business. Sports contracts continue to account for a large share of trading on the platform.

    In September, the platform introduced perpetual futures tied to precious metals such as gold and silver after it had originally filed in July to offer beyond prediction market event contracts with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal regulator overseeing derivatives contracts. Perpetual futures are futures-style contracts that have no expiration date.

    Kalshi also received approval to list perpetual futures tied to cryptocurrencies in late May.

    It has been revealed that the prediction market's stock trading offering was enabled by its purchase of broker-dealer FB Securities in July, the source said. FB Securities was founded in Delaware in 2024 and became registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission in December 2025. The broker did not respond to a request for comment.

    The Wall Street Journal first reported that Kalshi looks to introduce stock trading.

    Shares of Robinhood, which offers some prediction markets alongside equity trading, fell on Monday, though the stock was already lower amid a broader market sell-off. Robinhood closed down by 7.8%.

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    #15833. ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

    📅 05 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4140 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

    📅 05 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4140 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.
    • Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.
    • The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

    Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

    The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

    But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the latest season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he stated.

    It has been revealed that “We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

    “All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”.

    Industry observers note that despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”.

    Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

    The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

    Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

    It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

    But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

    Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” remarked Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

    Recent findings suggest that “We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”.

    Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

    He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

    Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

    In a recent development, if Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

    Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

    The fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”.

    🌴 @RealBetis_en's Hector Bellerin reacts to a 3-1 preseason win over his former club Arsenal"I spent 10 years over there always trying to help and see Arsenal where it belongs, and it's nice to finally face them with them being in that position" 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/er3YtAysQb.

    August 1- Girona 1 Arsenal 4Today- Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3August 9- Arsenal vs Borussia DortmundAugust 12- Arsenal vs ComoAugust 16- Arsenal vs Manchester City (Community Shield).

    It has been revealed that “It is another opportunity for fitness. Coming into games against teams of good quality, it is important we get good fitness. It is a chance to build momentum for the season ahead. We are taking steps in the right direction. Of course, we want more from the performance and the results, but we take learnings and move on.

    According to recent reports, “All of us, together, we share a common goal. We have confidence to build on. We will take every game as it comes. The atmosphere was amazing. I did not realise Ireland has so many Arsenal fans. We are so grateful for everyone who came to support us today. We wanted to give them a good result and performance. Hopefully next time we can.”.

    “We always want to win and in the end we could not today. In some ways they deserved it and we could have done better. We did have some good moments though. We had an amazing season last season. I believe in this team and there are still players to come back from the World Cup. I am confident but we can always do better.”.

    Possession: Arsenal 56%-44% Real BetisShots: 9-10Shots on target: 2-7Corners: 2-2.

    It has been revealed that there is the final whistle in Dublin and Betis secure a 3-1 win over Arsenal at Aviva Stadium. Goals from Riquelme, Deossa and Fornals has led Manuel Pellegrini’s side to the victory. All four goals in the game came before the break.

    And that's full time in Dublin 👏Real Betis claim a 3-1 win against Premier League champions Arsenal 🌴 pic.twitter.com/0XWByNdtgh.

    Jesus gets onto the end of a ball in behind, getting to it just before the byline, and delivers a dangerous cross but Natan does well on the stretch to clear.

    There will be three added minutes.

    Antony was booed when he came on and is also being booed whenever he touches the ball.

    Sources indicate that arsenal have registered just two shots on target in this game and both of those came in the first half. They have not really looked like scoring since the break, with probably Jesus coming closest.

    Double change for Betis as Morante and Gomez replace Riquelme and Bernal.

    Bellerin squares the ball from the byline and picks out Riquelme near the penalty spot but the latter is unable to take advantage.

    The changes keep coming for Arsenal as Gabriel and Martinelli, who have only recently returned from their breaks after the World Cup, go off after half an hour on the pitch. Nwaneri was the final member of the Arsenal starting XI to still be on but his night is over.

    Up until this point, Manuel Pellegrini had made just one change but he now makes a triple substitution, which sees three former Premier League players come on. Former Leeds duo Firpo and Llorente come on as does ex-Manchester United forward Antony. There are a few boos from the Arsenal fans as Antony comes on.

    It has been revealed that martinelli is played in down the left channel and gets onto the end of the ball inside the Betis box. He checks back and finds his compatriot Jesus on the edge of the box. Jesus tries to pick out the bottom corner but his shot goes just wide.

    Isco should put Betis 4-1 up but tries to be too cute and clever. Former Arsenal man Bellerin delivers a cross from the right side of the box and picks out a free Isco in the six-yard box. Isco attempts an audacious flick rather than putting his foot through it and his effort is saved by Meslier. That should have been a goal.

    Arsenal have changed nearly their entire starting XI whereas Betis have made just the one substitution thus far. Betis have played more games so far in pre-season, which probably explains the difference in the number of changes.

    Salmon is deceived by a dummy by Riquelme and then brings the Betis man down, earning him a yellow card.

    In a recent development, on the hour mark, Mikel Arteta is going to make a triple change, which feels like it was a plan going into the game. That includes Meslier coming on in goal in place of Kepa.

    Copley is helped off by the two Arsenal medics, shaking his head and not putting any weight on his left leg, and is replaced by Julienne.

    You have to hope that the knee injury to Louie Copley is not serious but judging by the way he went down largely unchallenged, his reaction and the way he was being helped down the tunnel it didn’t look too good. A tough moment for the youngster who had only been on the pitch nine minutes.

    In a recent development, play is halted as Copley has been down for a little while clutching at his left knee. He got his studs stuck in the ground and went down in some pain. The medics come on to check that left knee. He only came on at half-time but his night is over not even 10 minutes into the second half.

    Nwaneri catches Bernal and if this was a competitive fixture than I think Nwaneri would perhaps have been booked for that challenge.

    Those raft of changes from Mikel Arteta at half-time have seen just four of their starting XI remain on the pitch; Kepa, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly and Nwaneri.

    Arsenal have a corner early on in this second half as Vieira’s shot from distance deflects behind. The delivery from the left has too much on it, going over the heads of all the Arsenal players in the box, and Betis are able to clear.

    Mikel Arteta has made a whole host of changes, which includes the likes of Jesus, Martinelli, Gabriel and Vieira coming on. Betis have brought the former Real Madrid man Isco on at the break.

    We are back under way in Dublin.

    Possession: Arsenal 63%-37% Real BetisShots: 5-7Shots on target: 2-6Corners: 1-2.

    Industry observers note that arsenal’s title triumph was built on that stout defence and conceding so few but there have been so many self-inflicted wounds here. The first and third goals came from dismal individual errors from Kepa and Havertz and the second - while a wonder strike - came after Arsenal had failed to clear their lines properly.

    The first half is brought to an end and Real Betis take a 3-1 lead into the break.

    There will be one added minute.

    In a recent development, manuel Pellegrini’s side have their third goal of the night and restore their two-goal advantage. Havertz gives the ball away poorly deep inside his own half and the ball is played into Fornals. The former West Ham man has it on the edge of the box and has P Garcia in space to his right but opts to shoot. It is a clinical finish from Fornals as he picks out the bottom left corner and celebrates by crossing his arms to form irons, paying tribute to his days at West Ham.

    "It's so so easy!" 🎙️The former West Ham man Pablo Fornals puts Real Betis 3-1 up against Arsenal 🌴🔨 pic.twitter.com/iyBeyS1nHd.

    Betis come close to restoring their two-goal advantage. Calafiori gives the ball away deep inside his own half and the ball is quickly moved onto P Garcia on the right side of the box. He opens up his body and curls a shot first time towards the far corner, forcing Kepa into the save down to his right.

    Riquelme shoots from just outside the box and forces Kepa into a save down to his right.

    Recent findings suggest that betis have one goal from a corner and now Arsenal do. Betis keeper Valles complains that he is being fouled by Havertz after Tzolis swung in the corner from the left and the ball comes through to Hincapie, who has the simplest of headers from inside the six-yard box.

    Normal service is resumed with a Gunners goal from the corner 👏Piero Hincapié gives the @Arsenal fans reason to celebrate! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/b7h979i0Gv.

    It has been revealed that crucial block from P Garcia. Dowman cuts in from the right across the face of the penalty area and finds Tzolis in space to his left. Tzolis takes one touch before taking on the shot from inside the Betis box but P Garcia slides in with a crucial block.

    According to recent reports, that is quite the finish! Deossa receives the ball in a central position around 25 yards out. He takes a couple of touches before lashing a shot with his left foot. His effort flies into the top corner and Betis have a 2-0 lead. Considering the quality of the finish, I am surprised that Deossa did not celebrate more bearing in mind you do not score screamers like that every day!

    Recent findings suggest that nelson Deossa...what a hit! 😱😱Real Betis double their lead over Arsenal with a stunning strike and Mikel Arteta doesn't look happy 🌴 pic.twitter.com/4J5QnjOury.

    Since Gyokeres misses that very good chance just a minute into the game, Arsenal have not really carved out many genuine opportunities in front of goal, other than that Tzolis wasted chance. Every time they reach the final third, they are lacking that cutting edge.

    Calafiori’s role is interesting. He’s very nominally a left back but is routinely stepping into midfield and raiding forward, often ending up in positions you’d associate with a No. 10. It’s the kind of role Nico O’Reilly played under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City.

    Sources indicate that valles is so, so lucky. The Betis keeper inexplicably passes the ball straight at Tzolis inside the Betis penalty area but Tzolis is unable to capitalise. That is a huge slice of luck for Valles as that was a ridiculous moment.

    Sources indicate that betis have already scored one goal from a corner and they now have another corner after Nwaneri’s clearance behind. The inswinger is sent into a good area but this time Arsenal deal with the danger.

    Arsenal were the better side in the early stages but Betis have grown into this and have taken confidence from that goal.

    In a recent development, the first goal of the night goes the way of the Spaniards. The corner from the left should be dealt with by Kepa but the Arsenal keeper makes an absolute mess of it. The ball goes straight through him and comes to Riquelme at the far post. He takes one touch before firing into the net. Kepa is appealing for a free-kick but there is never a foul in there.

    According to recent reports, real Betis strike first at the Aviva! 🌴Riquelme takes advantage of poor Arsenal defending at the corner to open the scoring 👀 pic.twitter.com/1ubVDayElP.

    That is dire goalkeeping from Kepa. He’s desperately tried to claim he was fouled but he just made a complete hash of it.

    In a recent development, betis have their first shot of the night. P Garcia receives it out on the right and cuts inside onto his left. The space opens up for him to shoot and he obliges, forcing Kepa into a save before the ball is smashed behind for a corner...

    In a recent development, calafiori may be on the teamsheet tonight for Arsenal at left-back but when they are in possession the Italian is moving into midfield. Lewis-Skelly, who is playing in the number six role, is dropping in between the two centre-backs when Arsenal have the ball.

    Industry observers note that betis win a free-kick out on the left, with the chance to send it into the Arsenal penalty area for the first time tonight. It is clipped into a good area but Kepa is out of his goal to catch it.

    Recent findings suggest that arsenal should be ahead one minute into the game with their first attack of the game. Havertz picks up the ball on the corner of the box out on the left and passes it inside to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes one touch before shooting from the edge of the six-yard box but his shot is saved. In reality, Gyokeres should not have given Valles in the Betis goal any chance of saving that one.

    We are under way at Aviva Stadium.

    According to recent reports, both sides emerge from the tunnel, Arsenal led out by Ben White and Betis by former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin, and make their way past the Premier League trophy. We are moments away from kick-off in Dublin.

    In a recent development, “When I see the training and how hungry they are for every training drill, that means everybody is ready to compete at the highest level. When you are a player of Arsenal, you compete for every title that is possible. It is not only about the Premier League, it is about all the competitions we are playing for. I see a clear mindset and everything, that everybody is on the same page to win titles here. I saw it from the first training and I think when you train like that in the game, it makes it even better. I came here ready, with my fitness level and I was happy that I could show it here as well. I want to be myself and to show on the pitch all the passion and desire to win because I really like to win games and to give everything.

    “If I give 100% for every game and every duel, I think who does not like this? I think that is the best thing for a football player, and then you will always have the support from the supporters. I am thinking about how to improve and settle as fast as possible in the club, because I have the opportunity to train directly with the team from the beginning of the season, to play pre-season games and then to go to official games. This is a chance to play directly from the beginning and then it is up to me to show the qualities and what I can bring to the team. I am pretty confident I will show it in the next games.”.

    INS:Illan Meslier ⇠ Leeds, FreeChristos Tzolis ⇠ Club Brugge, £34m.

    Industry observers note that arsenal are closing in on the signing of Newcastle and Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimaraes in a deal worth £75m. One midfielder coming into Arsenal is set to see another depart as Dane Christian Norgaard closes in on a move to Everton after just one season at Arsenal.

    August 1- Girona 1 Arsenal 4Today- Arsenal vs Real BetisAugust 9- Arsenal vs Borussia DortmundAugust 12- Arsenal vs ComoAugust 16- Arsenal vs Manchester City (Community Shield).

    Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

    It has been revealed that arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

    Industry observers note that real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

    Industry observers note that they have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.
