    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade.
    • Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a company's ability to pay dividends consistently.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a company's ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The manufacturer has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

    In a recent development, in an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the company's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

    Specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

    Furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in latest wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

    "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," noted Mehta.

    Mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

    Kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream tech giant operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

    Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the organization to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

    According to recent reports, the 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

    Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

    "As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," said Mackay.

    Recent findings suggest that mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production tech giant with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent declared an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).

    Sources indicate that heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from fresh shares.

    "CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," said Richardson.

    The 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.

    Additionally, Richardson noted that the financial implications of the acquisition seem impressive, with a projected increase in cash flow per share of about 9% for 2027 to 2029.

    The analyst believes that Crescent is not just expanding its business through acquisitions but positioning itself as a more durable company, regardless of market conditions.

    Industry observers note that richardson ranks No. 478 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Crescent Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

    #15826. Jim Cramer says Costco's hefty special dividend signals ‘more gains ahead’

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (601 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Jim Cramer says Costco's hefty special dividend signals ‘more gains ahead’

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (601 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Costco is rewarding shareholders with a $30-per-share special dividend, and CNBC's Jim Cramer says history suggests that investors should stick around despite the catalyst moving into the rearview mirror.
    • The warehouse retailer unveiled its sixth special dividend last week, alongside a $4 billion share repurchase program.
    • It has been revealed that "With all due respect to the buyback program, which represents less than 1% of Costco's $490 billion market cap, it's the special dividend that I'm excited about," the "Mad Money" host stated.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Costco is rewarding shareholders with a $30-per-share special dividend, and CNBC's Jim Cramer says history suggests that investors should stick around despite the catalyst moving into the rearview mirror.

    The warehouse retailer unveiled its sixth special dividend last week, alongside a $4 billion share repurchase program. Shareholders of record as of Nov. 24 will receive the payout on Dec. 4. The organization also pays a regular quarterly dividend of $1.47 that yields just 0.5% annually.

    It has been revealed that "With all due respect to the buyback program, which represents less than 1% of Costco's $490 billion market cap, it's the special dividend that I'm excited about," the "Mad Money" host stated. "The sporadic special dividend is one of the unique privileges of owning Costco shares.".

    Industry observers note that costco issued its first special dividend in 2012 and has announced five more since then, with payouts arriving roughly every three years over the past decade. Together, those six payments have totaled $74 per share, on top of the company's regular quarterly dividend.

    According to recent reports, to be sure, given Costco's track record of these periodic extra payouts, some investors may view last week's announcement as a "buy the rumor, sell the news" situation. However, Cramer said in each of the past three instances — 2023, 2020 and 2017 — Costco shares have outperformed the S&P 500 over the next year.

    Industry observers note that "That's a very good verdict for those who wonder what to do with the stock now that the good news is out," Cramer said. "It claims hold on, don't sell. More gains ahead.".

    There's also compelling math suggesting that investors should look to reinvest those dividends back into Costco's stock.

    Cramer looked at investor returns over the past 15 years. A $1,000 investment in Costco's stock in November 2011 would have grown to approximately $13,321 through Friday, reflecting a 1,232% gain. But reinvesting all dividends into additional shares would have increased that investment's value to roughly $18,411, representing a 1,741% total return.

    Industry observers note that that's more than $5,000 in additional gains from reinvesting dividends rather than collecting the cash. Special dividends played an outsized role, accounting for roughly 64% of the $116 per share Costco paid in total dividends over that period. "That's an incredible case made for reinvesting of dividends," Cramer said.

    "The sporadic special dividends have boosted this stock's total shareholder return meaningfully over the past decade-and-a-half, and they help keep you invested in the stock when it has its occasional lulls," he said.

    In a recent development, beyond boosting returns, the prospect of another special dividend gives investors an incentive to hold Costco through periods of weakness. That patience paid off this year, when shares retreated from nearly $1,100 in May into the high $800s before rebounding sharply this fall. The stock is now up 30% for the year.

    According to recent reports, "Sometimes I think that the stock's too expensive and it might be a good time to take profits," he said. "But then I remind myself that there's a good chance of a special dividend right around the corner, and it's so much easier to stick it out.".

    #15821. Data center policy dominated the midterms. The 'Virginia of Europe' is the latest battleground

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (729 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Data center policy dominated the midterms. The 'Virginia of Europe' is the latest battleground

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (729 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Spain's government is seeking to tighten restrictions on one of Europe's fastest-growing data center booms, as the country's Socialist prime minister prepares to fight an election.
    • The measure, which doesn't need parliamentary approval, could be approved by Pedro Sánchez's cabinet by next week, and is widely expected to pass ahead of the Nov.
    • It could potentially cost one of Europe's fastest-growing tech regions billions of dollars in investment.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Spain's government is seeking to tighten restrictions on one of Europe's fastest-growing data center booms, as the country's Socialist prime minister prepares to fight an election. Investors like Amazon, Microsoft and Blackstone-backed QTS are on tenterhooks.

    The measure, which doesn't need parliamentary approval, could be approved by Pedro Sánchez's cabinet by next week, and is widely expected to pass ahead of the Nov. 29 elections.

    It could potentially cost one of Europe's fastest-growing tech regions billions of dollars in investment.

    Industry observers note that the government first introduced the decree in August, partly in response to concerns over energy demand and prices. After fierce opposition, it put forward a revised version on Oct. 26, but the proposal still includes strict renewable-energy requirements.

    "These requirements could pose insurmountable barriers and act as an effective moratorium," S&P remarked in an October report. The proposed rules would require 80% of electricity used by data centers to come from renewable sources matched hour by hour, with projects potentially losing grid access if they fail to comply.

    Projects already in development or awaiting grid connections would also be subject to the rules, with a five-year transition period to comply.

    Data center build-out has quickly become a prominent political issue around the world. In the U.S. midterm elections, CBS exit polls found data centers were a major influence for more than half of voters.

    In Spain, concerns over the water and energy demands of data centers are increasingly part of the election debate as the country faces mounting pressure to expand its electricity grid to meet the demand.

    CBRE estimates that while developers have announced 10.5 GW of data center capacity across Spain and Portugal, only about 4.5 GW is presently considered realistically deliverable because of grid, permitting and infrastructure constraints.

    Alberto Nadal, the opposition center-right Popular Party's deputy secretary for the economy, has mentioned a conservative government would repeal the decree. Recent polling indicates the Popular Party leading, with several seat projections putting the PP and far-right Vox together above a parliamentary majority.

    Aragón, a landlocked region in the country's northeast, governed by the Popular Party, has emerged as one of Europe's fastest-growing digital infrastructure hubs and is at the center of opposition to the draft rules.

    The region has attracted investors with fast-track permits, abundant renewable energy and land, and international cable connections. Aragón president, Jorge Azcón, wants to turn it into the "Virginia of Europe," referring to the U.S. state with the world's highest density of data center sites.

    Aragón is set to receive more than 60 billion euros ($66 billion) in data center and digital infrastructure investment over the next decade.

    But concerns are growing among residents over noise, water use and pressure on the electricity grid.

    Pilar Alegría, leader of the Socialist Party in Aragón, told a Nov. 15 rally that the election would be decisive for the region's future and for protecting its natural resources.

    She highlighted the Ebro River, which runs through Aragón, and raised concerns about the resources used by data centers in a region vulnerable to drought.

    Popular Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, speaking the same day, sought to reassure investors.

    "It would be a mistake to squander that advantage through poor planning or regulation that creates uncertainty for investors," Feijóo remarked.

    Eva Valle, Aragón's economy minister, has also called for the decree to be scrapped.

    "It is necessary to halt the approval of this decree, which abounds in harmful conditions placed on the sector," she mentioned at an AWS-organized event on Oct. 27, accusing the government of pursuing "a political agenda.".

    Amazon Web Services and Microsoft have stated their investment aims in Aragón remain unchanged, while urging Spain to provide long-term legal certainty and regulatory predictability.

    Recent findings suggest that google has already put a multibillion-euro data center project on hold pending greater regulatory certainty, according to a report in Spanish newspaper El Mundo, which cited anonymous sources. Google did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNBC.

    SpainDC, which represents the data-center industry in the country, stated the decree would give the group's members the most restrictive data center framework in the European Union and could put 80% to 90% of investment at risk.

    "We are going to use all the institutional, regulatory and legal avenues at our disposal" to challenge the decree, mentioned SpainDC president Emilio Díaz.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Sources indicate that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly key sources of transaction revenue, while the tech giant has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Recent findings suggest that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    Tech Report: U.S. companies from Nvidia to Apple face a growing China dilemma

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, BEIJING — How does the U.S.
    • businesses came into sharper focus after Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO, ahead of U.S.
    • Huang, who resigned last week amid reports he'd had an affair with a woman U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, BEIJING — How does the U.S. stay ahead of China in the artificial intelligence race? Keep advanced chips out of Beijing's reach, or sell weaker versions to keep Chinese companies reliant on American technology?

    The consequences for U.S. businesses came into sharper focus after Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO, ahead of U.S. President Donald Trump's meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping this week.

    Huang, who resigned last week amid reports he'd had an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy, had argued that keeping U.S. technology available in China could help the U.S. stay ahead in the tech race.

    Others want tougher restrictions on chip sales: The Trump administration tightened restrictions on Chinese companies' remote access to advanced U.S. chips on Monday, seeking to prevent them from bypassing export controls by using data centers overseas.

    Industry observers note that the question facing Nvidia is part of a broader dilemma for U.S. tech companies: how far to remain invested in China as tensions between the two countries put their access to customers and supply chains at risk.

    Industry observers note that on Sunday, nine countries, including Singapore and the U.K., signed the U.S. State Department's "San Francisco Declaration" to safeguard sensitive technologies.

    "Companies operating in China face competing pressures from Washington and Beijing," a client brief from New York-based consulting firm Strategy Risks stated following the Nvidia scandal.

    "Actions that satisfy one government can create serious problems with the other, putting market access, investments, and corporate reputation at risk," the brief said.

    "Executives need to understand and price out these trade-offs before making consequential decisions.".

    China's economic slowdown and escalating bilateral tensions have made it harder for American businesses there. Few expect Trump and XI to significantly expand on a fragile trade truce achieved last fall.

    In a recent development, huang was among the tech CEOs at the Xi-Trump summits in September and May, but U.S. officials mentioned Trump does not strategy to raise the alleged Nvidia spy case during Thursday's meeting. Elon Musk is travelling with the president, who is otherwise not bringing a business delegation as he did in May.

    "American tech companies have been diversifying away from China," Kyle Chan, a fellow at The Brookings Institution, told CNBC, but Nvidia and Apple are "in some ways stark outliers against this trend.".

    Analysts are watching how Apple CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook in October, navigates bilateral tensions.

    Sources indicate that "Ternus may accelerate a process of diversification away from China that Tim Cook started," Chan mentioned. "But it's hard to imagine that China will not play an essential role in Apple's future under Ternus, given the depth and breadth of China's manufacturing supply chains.".

    Apple still manufactures most of its iPhones in China, and Greater China, which Apple defines as mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan, accounts for around 15% of sales.

    "The most defensible path is managed decoupling—not the rolling deferrals and hedged announcements that defined Cook's tenure—but a genuine strategic commitment to building a firm that can absorb the reductions of China access without losing the ability to manufacture at the cutting edge," Strategy Risks CEO Isaac Stone Fish wrote in American Affairs earlier this year.

    China's economic clout, however, also increases the fallout from any retaliation Beijing decides to enact in response to tighter U.S. policy.

    Companies, especially U.S. multinationals, pursued the China market after it began re-opening to foreign businesses in the 1980s. Consumer demand boomed, while local factories produced so much they reached 40% of global container exports this summer. The U.S. AI data center buildout relied on China-made parts.

    In a recent development, china has amassed control of the supply chain for critical minerals. Beijing has used its grip on rare earths as leverage in trade talks with the U.S. and the EU.

    Despite some buildout of the rare earths supply outside China, "it's just not at the scale that the world needs to continue to build products and for industry to continue to evolve," mentioned Cameron Johnson, a Shanghai-based senior partner at business consultancy Tidalwave Solutions.

    He cited looming shortages of yttrium, which would limit the production and repair of airplane engines.

    Sources indicate that "There's just no road map. That's really one of the biggest issues," Johnson said. "Companies have no idea what they're ordering now, whether they will have access to it again.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.
    • Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick.
    • Industry observers note that just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side demonstrated some life late on.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

    Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

    Industry observers note that just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side demonstrated some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

    According to recent reports, aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

    It has been revealed that stepping up in the major moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR.

    Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

    Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

    Sources indicate that the final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

    The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

    It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

    There will be four added minutes.

    According to recent reports, when Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

    Gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

    It has been revealed that for 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

    Maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

    Industry observers note that abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

    Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

    Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

    Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

    Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

    A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

    In a recent development, bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

    According to recent reports, bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

    Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

    It has been revealed that that is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

    It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

    Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

    Sources indicate that should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

    Just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

    Recent findings suggest that good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

    Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

    Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

    Tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

    In a recent development, bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

    We are back under way in Hong Kong.

    There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

    Aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

    According to recent reports, the German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

    In a recent development, that is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

    Industry observers note that bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

    The first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

    That was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder reveals good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

    Bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

    Bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

    Industry observers note that aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is currently out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

    Industry observers note that the ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

    Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

    Good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

    The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

    Recent findings suggest that the first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

    Interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

    Industry observers note that both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

    Industry observers note that it has been a big summer of change at Aston Villa already and there could be more changes before the end of the window. Joao Palhinha, who is on the bench for Bayern Munich today, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa.

    “Aston Villa are a top side with a very good coach. They have a large squad and will field plenty of talent. They have already played more friendlies than us, but for us it is a good challenge. It is a match in which we will learn a lot about our team’s fitness. It will be a good match for us.”.

    “It is difficult to improve; after all, it is not just about the trophies we have won, but also about the number of goals and matches we have won. It is possible, but difficult.     In a recent development, aston Villa’s preparations for the new season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

    According to recent reports, after losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some newly introduced faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is at the moment on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

    In a recent development, unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

    According to recent reports, bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

    It has been revealed that after today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

    #15807. Analysis: The Fed's chairman sees an AI revolution coming. Now he has to figure out what it means

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (964 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Analysis: The Fed's chairman sees an AI revolution coming. Now he has to figure out what it means

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (964 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Artificial intelligence is about to sweep through the economy.
    • According to recent reports, "We are at a hinge point in the U.S.
    • The meeting of Warsh's AI task force saw the latest Fed chairman publicly asking the questions Americans will ultimately expect him to answer.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Artificial intelligence is about to sweep through the economy. The Federal Reserve is bracing for impact.

    According to recent reports, "We are at a hinge point in the U.S. economy," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh remarked at a conference he convened in San Francisco on Monday. But exactly when and how the economy could turn, and what that means for interest rates and inflation, isn't yet clear.

    The meeting of Warsh's AI task force saw the latest Fed chairman publicly asking the questions Americans will ultimately expect him to answer. He hinted at a few of his private views on whether white-collar workers could soon face massive job losses, but he largely left the speculation to an array of experts he has assembled to advise the Fed.

    It has been revealed that with the technology racing ahead, Warsh won't be able to put off giving his own answers much longer. AI lab Anthropic aims to price the shares for its initial public offering on Wednesday and could raise as much as $64 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation. Vast spending from AI firms is prompting the Fed to contemplate raising interest rates in December to slow down the rate of price increases as the tech sector heats up the economy.

    Meanwhile Americans are souring on some aspects of the technology. The Nov. 3 midterms saw voters enact an array of state-level measures to slow down construction of the data centers that are essential to powering AI.

    Warsh moderated three out of four sessions at Monday's event and was involved in selecting the speakers. Among them was one of the few prominent Democrats who was willing to speak out against that anti-data center trend.

    It is "a very troubling sign" that so many anti-data center measures passed in the midterms, Gina Raimondo said. She is a former secretary of commerce under President Joe Biden and a former governor of Rhode Island.

    Stopping AI "would be very bad for America" and for the people who voted for the measures, Raimondo said.

    Warsh didn't say whether he shares that view, and how it would translate into monetary policy isn't exactly clear.

    The event was an unusual one for the Fed. The central bank employs a small army of Ph.D. economists who can rapidly weigh in on anything affecting the U.S. and global economies. But in keeping with his longstanding critiques of the Fed as insular and outdated, Warsh has chosen to draw expertise from outside the institution to help it figure out how to think about what AI will do to productivity and jobs.

    Warsh has assembled a task force on that matter, alongside four others devoted to aspects of Fed policymaking.

    The public heard Monday from one of the three official members of the task force: venture capitalist Marc Andreessen. Warsh went to Stanford University with Andreessen's wife, and the two have been longtime friends. Another task force member, Stanford economist Chad Jones, is on leave and working at Anthropic and couldn't speak during the company's blackout period ahead of the IPO. The third, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, didn't attend the event.

    Andreessen is hugely optimistic about the promise of AI as a technology, but believes the government won't let Americans experience its full effects. Heavy regulation in areas such as healthcare and education mean technology can't replace people's jobs in those sectors, he said.

    "To the extent our economy is a free-market economy, then maybe you could see the, let's say, extremely rapid displacement scenarios people are talking about," Andreessen mentioned. "But we've mostly outlawed the kind of job transition that … both the utopians the doomers talk about.".

    Warsh returned repeatedly to one scenario for the economy that draws on past experience. The so-called China shock unfolded after that country joined the World Trade Organization in 2001 and moved heavily into low-cost manufacturing. Americans saw prices on clothing and furniture drop rapidly, for instance, but at the cost of severe job losses. One widely cited estimate found the U.S. lost a million manufacturing jobs and 2.4 million jobs overall in the years that followed.

    Warsh suggested to one of the panelists that the widespread adoption of AI might produce its own version of the China shock, this time focused on service workers.

    "I don't want to hold this too tightly," Warsh remarked. "But if in some ways over the last generation or generation and a half, the China shock, for lack of a better word, lowered prices of goods in the United States, the way that I heard you talking about the philosophy of this fresh technology is it might do something for services.".

    It has been revealed that in other words, AI could do, say, legal or administrative work more cheaply than a human. That could lower prices but put many people out of a job.

    Warsh asked panelists whether "we should expect disinflation over the medium term, from what AI could do to services.".

    They largely suggested it was possible, which could mean the Fed might eventually want to lower interest rates over the long term.

    But at the end of the day, it is Warsh and his fellow Fed members who will need to have conviction on the answer.

    Industry observers note that there are still many steps between the task force discussion and any kind of change in Fed policy. First, the three task force members will have to assemble their points of view into a report for Warsh sometime in the next few months. Then the Fed itself will need to debate those results and decide whether or how to use them to shape monetary policy.

    But with AI growing bigger every day, the Fed may need to make up its mind sooner rather than later.

    Berkshire Hathaway raised its stake in Delta in the third quarter. It also trimmed a key bank holding

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (329 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Berkshire Hathaway made several moves in the stock market during the third quarter, adding to key positions and trimming others.
    • Recent findings suggest that the Omaha-based conglomerate, now led by CEO Greg Abel, increased its Delta Air Lines stake by 12%, scooping up 7.13 million shares.
    • Abel succeeded legendary investor Warren Buffett, 96, at the start of this year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Berkshire Hathaway made several moves in the stock market during the third quarter, adding to key positions and trimming others.

    Recent findings suggest that the Omaha-based conglomerate, now led by CEO Greg Abel, increased its Delta Air Lines stake by 12%, scooping up 7.13 million shares. The position was worth $5.37 billion at the end of the third quarter.

    Abel succeeded legendary investor Warren Buffett, 96, at the start of this year. Buffett continues to control roughly 13% of Berkshire common stock, Reuters mentioned Monday, after the former CEO donated $5.5 billion to nonprofit foundations.

    According to recent reports, berkshire boosted its stake in Delta as the Atlanta-based carrier's shares tumbled 11% in the third quarter, hurt by rising jet fuel prices due to the U.S.-Iran war that pressured the entire airline industry. That marked the stock's worst quarterly performance since the first quarter of 2025, when it plunged 28%. Delta last month also cut its full-year earnings forecast, citing a surge in fuel costs.

    It has been revealed that to be sure, buying that dip has been a winning investment thus far. Delta is up 3.8% so far in the fourth quarter, while the S&P 500 has dropped 3.1%. Shares are also up nearly 15% over the past month.

    Berkshire also trimmed its holding in Bank of America by nearly 6%, selling more than $1.6 billion worth of stock.

    BofA was under pressure in the third quarter, falling more than 4%, as interest rates surged alongside stubbornly high inflation and expectations of tighter Federal Reserve monetary policy. At one point in September the 30-year Treasury bond yield surged above 5.6% to its highest level since 2002.

    Despite the share sale, Bank of America remains a top Berkshire Hathaway holding, with the conglomerate's stake valued at $24.8 billion at the end of the third quarter.

    Berkshire also initiated a position in Bending Spoons and nearly doubled its stake in homebuilder Lennar in the latest quarter.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the ongoing earnings season, Middle East tensions and buzz ahead of the U.S. midterm elections have been keeping investors busy. Further, worries about elevated artificial intelligence spending are weighing on investor sentiment.

    Investors looking beyond the short-term noise and focusing on long-term returns can track top Wall Street analysts to pick the right stocks, backed by strong research.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    This week's first stock pick is Datadog, an AI-powered observability and security platform. The company will announce its results for the third quarter on Nov. 4. Datadog is seeing strong demand for its offerings, thanks to cloud migration and rapid AI adoption. TipRanks' KPIs tool for DDOG indicates the growth in its customer base over the past few years amid increasing market penetration and growing adoption of its products.

    Heading into Q3 FY26 earnings, Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda reiterated a buy rating on Datadog stock and raised his price target to $335 from $305. The analyst noted that industry checks and data indicate that infrastructure software demand is strengthening, with AI increasingly driving usage and growth.

    Ikeda called Datadog and Atlassian his top picks, saying that companies that can show that AI is a tailwind to growth could see their valuation rerate, even at premium multiples. He added that the total addressable market for observability is growing faster than anticipated, driven by accelerated growth of enterprise AI and the rapid ramp of consumer AI agents.

    The five-star analyst believes that focus will be on revenue growth, which he estimates to be 28.7% for Q3 FY26 versus the Street's consensus of 29.1%. Ikeda thinks that the market is underestimating the growth prospects of DDOG's security products. Meanwhile, he cautioned investors about concentration risk related to large customers.

    "We think results will be supportive of our long-term thesis that Datadog is a strong share gainer in the rapidly expanding observability opportunity," said Ikeda.

    Ikeda ranks No. 673 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 55% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.9%. See Datadog Statistics on TipRanks.

    The next pick, semiconductor giant Nvidia, is also benefiting from AI-driven demand for its products. After attending Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore reaffirmed a buy rating on NVDA stock with a price target of $300, calling it a top pick in the semiconductor space.

    Industry observers note that the five-star analyst noted that the conference supported his thesis that Nvidia continues to effectively navigate bottlenecks in the supply chain, land/power/shell, and funding. In fact, Moore is "convinced that all 3 aspects are opportunities for NVDA.".

    According to recent reports, while Nvidia's GTC Berlin offered no major updates, Moore noted the conference reflected that the company continues to add to its significant advantages heading into 2027. The analyst said that Vera Rubin is gaining momentum, though details on next year's Rubin Ultra were lighter than expected.

    In a recent development, with demand outpacing supply, Moore said that focus is on closing the gap. In this regard, he highlighted the supply chain deals on substrate, packaging and testing. While the analyst continues to view TSMC 3 nm wafer supply as the biggest challenge, he expects it to ease over time.

    Industry observers note that moore ranks No. 142 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 23.4%. See Nvidia Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Aerospace company SpaceX recently confirmed solid third-quarter results, with its AI revenue surging to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the prior-year quarter.

    Impressed by the results, Needham analyst Ryan Koontz reiterated a buy rating on SPCX stock with a price target of $250. Koontz highlighted that SpaceX's Q3 results significantly exceeded expectations, proving that the firm's vertically integrated business model is driving massive scale.

    According to recent reports, furthermore, Koontz emphasized the 195.2% sequential growth in SpaceX's AI revenue, fueled by wholesale spot compute deals. He noted management's increasing focus on its AI strategy, given that it is optimistic about adding 10 gigawatts of incremental capacity during 2027.

    "With increasing confidence on Starship re-use, we meaningfully increase our estimates," said Koontz.

    Industry observers note that koontz ranks No. 357 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 42% of the time, delivering an average return of 23.7%. See SpaceX Technical Analysis on TipRanks.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Vice President JD Vance said Monday he will make a decision next year about whether to run for president in 2028.
    • "We'll figure it out sometime next year," he told Fox News host Laura Ingraham in an interview that aired Monday evening.
    • According to recent reports, "I'm not an expert in this but my understanding with a presidential campaign is there's a lot of infrastructure that you have to set up, fundraising, all that stuff and so you can't declare a month before the Iowa caucus that you're going to run for president," he mentioned.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    U.S. Vice President JD Vance said Monday he will make a decision next year about whether to run for president in 2028.

    "We'll figure it out sometime next year," he told Fox News host Laura Ingraham in an interview that aired Monday evening.

    According to recent reports, "I'm not an expert in this but my understanding with a presidential campaign is there's a lot of infrastructure that you have to set up, fundraising, all that stuff and so you can't declare a month before the Iowa caucus that you're going to run for president," he mentioned. "So, you know, I haven't made a decision.".

    Vance has yet to openly declare any ambition to succeed President Donald Trump when his current term ends, but speculation that the vice president has his sights set on the White House has been mounting for some time. In the wake of the GOP's crushing defeat in the U.S. midterm election on Nov. 3, anonymous sources involved in campaigns told Reuters Vance was among the high-profile Republicans who had begun early preparations for a 2028 run.

    Candidates typically announce their intentions to run in the election in the spring of 2027, with parties holding nominating conventions to formally select their presidential candidates between July and September.

    It has been revealed that polymarket at the moment slates Vance as the frontrunner to win the Republican presidential nomination for the 2028 election, with the prediction market giving him a 37% chance of becoming the nominee. Kalshi currently gives a 73% chance that Vance will run for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination. Odds and gambling platforms do not use methodologies used by traditional political polling, and therefore are not substitutes for political polls.

    Pressed on 2028 in Monday's interview, Vance said: "When I make a decision, I will be all in on whatever that decision is.".

    Candidates vying for the Republican nomination face the challenge of convincing voters the party can veer away from unpopular Trump-era policies without alienating its MAGA base.

    Vance himself has blamed the Iran war for the midterm election outcome.

    According to recent reports, "I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, "I told you so": you're right, you did tell us so," he said in a lengthy X post as the results were coming in. "Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let's take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.".

    In his interview with Fox News on Monday, Vance said the Republicans got "shellacked" in the midterms.

    "We have to take messages from that, but the message that we have to take is that the American people want prosperity, they want freedom, they want sovereignty within their own country and they want us to do more of the good things that we've done," he said.

    He added that lawmakers needed to double down on "economic nationalism" and bring "prosperity to the homeland" to deal with "economic pain" in the United States.

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, iran has ratcheted up threats against U.S.
    • Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy warned shipping companies against using the U.S.-backed southern route through the Strait of Hormuz, describing it as fully closed and a "minefield of fire," according to regional media outlets citing a statement from the force.
    • Mohammad Akrami-Nia, a spokesperson for the Iranian Army, remarked the Strait of Hormuz would not reopen until "the enemy accepts Iran's conditions.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, iran has ratcheted up threats against U.S. forces and commercial shipping as a third American aircraft carrier arrived in the Gulf, stoking fears of renewed escalation in the nine-month conflict.

    Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy warned shipping companies against using the U.S.-backed southern route through the Strait of Hormuz, describing it as fully closed and a "minefield of fire," according to regional media outlets citing a statement from the force.

    Brig. Gen. Mohammad Akrami-Nia, a spokesperson for the Iranian Army, remarked the Strait of Hormuz would not reopen until "the enemy accepts Iran's conditions.".

    Separately, CNN reported Monday that latest U.S. intelligence indicated Iran was developing prepares that could target senior Trump administration officials with a so-called dirty bomb, or a chemical weapon in Washington, D.C. CNBC cannot immediately verify the report.

    The intelligence was characterized as an effort by Iran to develop options rather than evidence of an imminent attack, CNN reported. U.S. officials have held several meetings over the past week to consider how to respond to the potential threat.

    The heightened security concerns come after Iranian threats prompted Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to relocate to military housing last week.

    "We remain vigilant, monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland," a White House spokesperson mentioned in a statement to CNBC.

    Recent findings suggest that oil prices inched lower in Asian trading Tuesday, with international benchmark Brent crude futures dropping 0.7% to $91.8 a barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures falling 0.7% to $85.1 a barrel.

    On Tuesday, the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations mentioned a tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz and subsequently caught fire. The agency did not say who was responsible and urged vessels to transit with caution and report suspicious activity.

    Separately, the Iranian navy noted four oil tankers had struck mines and caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz over the previous 24 hours.

    Recent findings suggest that the escalation in Tehran's rhetoric came as the USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived in the Gulf region on Sunday, joining the USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington. That added to U.S. firepower near Iran even as President Donald Trump stated the war was winding down.

    Trump has sent mixed signals regarding the conflict in recent weeks, alternating between declaring it could soon end and warning of renewed large-scale strikes if efforts to reach a deal fail.

    After meeting Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani last week, Trump remarked the war with Iran could end "fairly soon," adding that it "militarily is effectively over.".

    Industry observers note that tehran said Sunday that it launched six drones at a U.S. air-defense radar at Bahrain's Riffa air base, the second attack Iran claimed against the kingdom in three days. Bahrain's military said it intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks.

    Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned the attacks in a call Monday with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani and reaffirmed Washington's commitment to the security of Bahrain and other Gulf partners.

    Industry observers note that the conflict began in late February when the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran, prompting Tehran to retaliate with strikes on Israel and Gulf states hosting American military bases. Indirect talks between Washington and Tehran through Qatar have since appeared to run into a stalemate as warring powers disagreed over terms to reach a lasting peace deal.

    Washington appears unwilling to accept several of Iran's demands to end the war, including lifting the U.S. naval blockade on its southern ports and lifting sanctions, while stressing that Iran cannot possess a nuclear weapon.

    Iran is likely to continue escalating attacks on tankers and container ships, along with occasional strikes on U.S. military targets, in an effort to pressure Washington into offering concessions, remarked Ian Bremmer, president and founder of Eurasia Group. In response, Washington will likely expand its blockade on Iran's maritime and inland trade routes, he said.

    "The presumption is that eventually Iran can't handle the economic pressure and will accept better terms," Bremmer stated, calling that view a "misread of the Iranian leadership and their capacity to resist.".

    Over the coming year, Iran is likely to intensify efforts to disrupt shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, Bremmer said.

    The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

    The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

    Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

    Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have newly introduced managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

    Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

    According to recent reports, “We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso remarked in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so key to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”.

    It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

    AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their major-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

    Sources indicate that how do all 32 teams in the NHL compare? Who has eyes set on the Stanley Cup? Who is treading water hoping for better days past this season?

    Recent findings suggest that as the regular season progresses, we’ll evaluate how the 32 teams move up and down with updated NHL power rankings each week. Let’s evaluate the League, ranking the teams from No. 32 to No. 1, after the week ending Nov. 16.

    It has been revealed that not even having Logan Cooley back could prevent Utah from reaching straight losses (0-3-3) by falling to Vancouver on Monday, when the Mammoth were still without Nick Schmaltz. Before missing the previous three games with an upper-body injury, Cooley had 10 goals in the prior eight games. Schmaltz, who has been sidelined the past three games with a lower-body injury, has 20 points (nine goals, 11 assists) in 19 games this season. Missing each of them has drastically cooled what was a redhot team just a few weeks ago.

    Chicago seemed primed to bounce back from a dysmal showing the prior week. After a 9-2 drubbing at the hands of the Carolina Hurricanes on Nov. 7 capped a six-game losing streak (0-5-1), the Blackhawks reset with a four-day break and scratched out a 3-2 overtime win over the Buffalo Sabres on Thursday. Then, they were up 4-0 in the second period against the Winnipeg Jets on Saturday. All the good will evaporated when Winnipeg scored four straight and beat Chicago 5-4 in a shootout. Connor Bedard does have 17 points (six goals, 11 assists) in 14 games, though. So, that’s nice.

    The Kings have never really gotten started this season, but have particularly flatlined lately. They beat the San Jose Sharks 7-2 on Nov. 4 and have scored a combined six goals in four consecutive losses since. Los Angeles wasn’t at all competitive during that stretch until Saturday, when Matvei Gridin scored the winning goal at 11:21 of the third period for the Calgary Flames in a 3-2 defeat of the Kings. Before that, they were handled 5-2 by the Pittsburgh Penguins on Nov. 7, 3-0 by the Nashville Predators on Tuesday and 5-2 by the New York Islanders on Thursday.

    Industry observers note that trade rumors surrounding star forward Matvei Michkov clouded what was otherwise an OK week in Philadelphia. There was a lopsided 5-2 loss to the Edmonton Oilers on Sunday, but it’s hard to hold that against the Flyers. They came into that one with points in their previous four games (2-0-2) and Michkov scored a highlight-reel breakaway goal as Philadelphia bested the Columbus Blue Jackets 4-3 on Saturday. General manager Danny Briere has denied the Michkov rumors, but that won’t keep them from being another unneeded distraction.

    Columbus has fallen rapidly since an extremely promising start to November. It blew out the Colorado Avalanche 7-2 to start the month on Nov. 3 and topped the Dallas Stars 2-1 in a shootout two days later. It’s been outscored 16-7 in four straight losses since with the last three coming at home. The Blue Jackets do have a golden chance to get right this week with games against the New York Islanders on Tuesday, the Blackhawks on Thursday and the Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday. But they can probably be counted as buried if the skid continues.

    It has been revealed that how bad are things for the Maple Leafs? They held the Oilers to just a single goal on Saturday and somehow still lost. Falling 1-0 to Edmonton is the latest of six straight losses to start November. Toronto allowed at least four goals in each of the previous four losses and at least three in the previous five. Auston Matthews suddenly has just one goal in his past six games and Gavin McKenna is still finding his footing with two points (one goal, one assist) in his past seven.

    According to recent reports, sergei Murashov provided some hope by starting three of the past four games. The 22-year-old goalie helped steady Pittsburgh with 26 saves in a 5-2 win over the Kings on Nov. 7 before Arturs Silovs took over in a for a 5-2 loss at the Anaheim Ducks the next day. Murashov returned with 34 saves in a 3-2 shootout win at the Sharks on Wednesday and was solid on Saturday with 30 saves against the Ottawa Senators. The problem? Pittsburgh’s defense is abysmal, seemingly giving up a 2-on-1 one minute and a breakaway the next. So, the Penguins lost 4-1 to the Senators. It also doesn’t help that the power play didn’t record a single shot on goal on three chances.

    According to recent reports, kudos to Daniil Tarasov for getting Detroit off the schneid, making 31 saves in a 2-0 win over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Saturday for his second shutout in seven starts this season. The Red Wings had lost five in a row. Tarasov has been an obvious bright spot in what’s otherwise been a dark start to the season in Hockeytown. He is just 3-3-2, but has a 1.84 goals-against average and .931 save percentage. Detroit could do much more to help him with just 18 goals in his nine games.

The Flames haven’t been terrible with points in four of seven games this month (3-3-1), but it’s hard to see them as anything more than a team with a very interesting goalie.

But these budding Sharks still have enough runway to make noise.

    Sources indicate that the Sabres have fallen off completely since ending October with three straight wins. A 5-2 defeat of the Blue Jackets is the only victory in six games this month (1-4-1). On Saturday, Buffalo had just 22 shots on goal — with 11 coming in the third period — in a 2-0 loss to the Dallas Stars.
