    #15785. Anthropic IPO: For hundreds of billions of dollars flowing into AI startups, a significant debut is a must

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1492 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic IPO: For hundreds of billions of dollars flowing into AI startups, a significant debut is a must

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1492 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Artificial intelligence has propelled substantial gains in venture capital funds this year, and a flood of money — over $350 billion — into AI startups.
    • Sources indicate that it has been a period of increased volatility for tech stocks and the public market AI trade.
    • But on the private side of tech investing, firms are closely watching how investors react to Anthropic's IPO.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Artificial intelligence has propelled substantial gains in venture capital funds this year, and a flood of money — over $350 billion — into AI startups. Venture funds were up close to 18% through the first half of 2026, with 86% of U.S.-based VC investor money going into AI companies. With Anthropic set to make its public market debut this week at a reported valuation of $1.4 trillion, the market's reception to the deal and early trading in its shares may set the tone for the next leg in the private market AI boom.

    Sources indicate that it has been a period of increased volatility for tech stocks and the public market AI trade. In addition to concerns about balance sheet strength and valuation, midterm elections revealed widespread public opposition to data centers, and the CEO scandal rocking Nvidia, the "central bank" of AI financing, has compounded risks in the sector.

    But on the private side of tech investing, firms are closely watching how investors react to Anthropic's IPO. "I think that will end up guiding further intentions for the VC space," mentioned Mike McLelland, managing director of investments within private markets at Cleveland, Ohio-based Clearstead. "Once you have a couple of good exits, it gives people a little more confidence in the realization story.".

    Read more: Everything you need to know about the Anthropic IPO.

    Anthropic is getting some deep-pocketed support for the deal. Altimeter Capital is aiming to invest $5 billion, according to its founder and CEO Brad Gerstner, who noted that was five times as much as he has ever invested in an IPO. "I think this is a cornerstone compounder for a long time," Gerstner told CNBC's "Halftime Report" on Monday. "It's where the trade is going.".

    Chip giants Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Nvidia, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Organization and Micron are all investing, as are Google and Microsoft.

    Industry observers note that the direction of the IPO market is crucial given that companies have been staying private longer than they did in the past and strategic exits have been relatively muted, McLelland stated. A notable exception is Google's $32 billion acquisition of cloud security firm Wiz. That 2025 deal was Google's largest ever, overtaking its $12.5 billion purchase of Motorola in 2012.

    It has been revealed that VC gains have been concentrated in a small number of large funds that hold the biggest AI-linked companies. MSCI reports that the 10 largest holdings make up 22% of the value of its venture index.

    That concentration comes amid improved performance.

    According to recent reports, venture capital funds returned 17.8% in the first six months of 2026, according to Opto Investments, using proprietary and MSCI Private Capital Solutions data. Venture fund portfolio data is reported by fund general partners on a delayed basis. The six-month gains would equate to a full year return as high as 38% if the pace is maintained. It comes on the heels of a recent period of underperformance for the asset class, with a 6.19% return over five years, according to Juan Mier, lead analyst of fund strategies at PitchBook. Venture's 10-year average return is 13% annually, according to PitchBook. For the year ended March 2026, venture capital delivered a nearly 22% return, driven in large part by AI valuations, Mier mentioned.

    In a recent development, it is not just the largest AI companies that are venture-backed and tied to the IPO performance of the giants. Thousands of smaller companies that supply AI giants with infrastructure, component manufacturing, and data services, for example, have also seen their valuations rise swiftly, remarked Jake Miller, co-founder of Latest York-based Opto Investments, which helps investment advisors design private investment programs.

    Notably, AI captured $355.9 billion, or 86% of U.S. venture dollars in the first half of 2026, according to Clearstead analysis of PitchBook data. Globally, AI deal value reached $521.4 billion over the trailing twelve months. That's more than double the prior year, even as AI deal count fell 21.6% from the previous quarter.

    Mier noted venture capital returns are expected to moderate in the third quarter as valuations in the AI space in public markets have adjusted, and that flows to private markets eventually. "That may moderate returns for the second half of the year," he said. Anthropic's deal, reported to be on target for a $1.4 trillion valuation, is well below the $2 trillion deal value originally floated by bankers.

    But amid the AI proliferation, industry participants expect VC to continue piquing investors' interest in the coming years. "It's been a great place to be, and it's going to be a great place to be given the momentum of venture companies," stated Jeff Masom, head of U.S. distribution and global wealth management for private markets at Franklin Templeton, which manages several private markets investments.

    Industry observers note that that remarked, some investors are getting more discerning. "We see those opportunities among early-stage — Seed, Series A and Series B — companies rather than trying to get in on a later-stage company at a higher price," said Opto Investments' Miller. He's looking for opportunities to buy stakes in lower-valuation companies that could climb 10 times to 20 times from their current value through an IPO or acquisition.

    Industry observers note that private infrastructure, meanwhile, returned 4.2% over the first six months of the year, a pace of about 8.5% a year, according to Opto Investments and MSCI data. "That is close to infrastructure's 10-year average of just under 10% a year," remarked Miller, but good enough to be the second-best among major private fund categories through the first half of 2026, ahead of private credit (2.6%) and buyout funds (1.4%). Private credit has been hit hard by fears about lending to software companies that could be rendered uncompetitive by AI, while private equity funds have struggled to sell portfolio companies at a profit this year, with a huge backlog of portfolio holdings.

    Sources indicate that but the AI boom has also benefited investors in infrastructure funds, given the needs for power, data centers, and fiber, areas where activity has been the strongest. "It's what's been driving most of those returns in the last 18 months or so," stated Uday Karri, a member of MSCI's Private Capital Research team.

    In a recent development, A recent MSCI report on private infrastructure showed that the index returned 11.9% over the 12 months through June 2026, compared with 7.7% for the median asset. Returns are based on MSCI's asset-level index, which measures underlying asset performance before fund fees, according to a spokesperson.

    According to recent reports, there's been tremendous growth in the past few quarters within infrastructure, and there continue to be opportunities for investors in the asset class, especially in AI-ready and liquid-cooled data centers, he mentioned. Of course, midterm elections could slow newly introduced data center development through tighter permitting and regulation. In Texas, for example, Democratic governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on a statewide moratorium on new data center permits. Shortly after her election, the new governor stressed in an interview with CNN that the key is creating state laws that protect Texas communities, not banning data centers.

    Recent findings suggest that with more political pressure related to data center construction, the infrastructure sector may benefit from expected opportunities outside the AI infrastructure build-out over the next several years. "Power, grid connections, water, cooling, fiber, and permitting are likely to shape where capacity can be delivered. Shifting trade routes, geopolitical disruption, and more frequent extreme weather are supporting investment in ports, railways, intermodal terminals, cold-storage networks, and other strategic transport infrastructure," according to a report from BlackRock's Preqin division.

    Legislation is also advancing that could raise project costs for the biggest data centers, but potentially have more positive impacts on broader infrastructure projects. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), a sweeping bill on energy infrastructure, is "the most comprehensive permitting bill to date," according to The Bipartisan Policy Center. If passed, it is expected to increase the speed of project permitting and reduce delays.

    In a recent development, here too, investors need to be discerning. "For investors, the key point is that asset selection can matter more than regional allocation. Larger portfolios can spread this dispersion across many assets and are more likely to track the index. Smaller portfolios hold fewer assets, so their results may differ materially from the index in either direction," MSCI wrote.

    Private credit did perform better over the trailing 12 months ending in March, 8.3%, while real estate debt and core-plus strategies returned 7.2% and 5.1%, respectively, according to data from Preqin.

    Industry observers note that "The broader takeaway is that private markets are not moving in lockstep," Pei Yin, director at Preqin Private Markets Research, said in an email. "Venture capital has shown stronger return momentum, infrastructure continues to benefit from long-term investment themes, while private credit and selected real estate strategies have offered more income-oriented sources of return.".

    #15783. Roth 401(k) matches are 'surging,' report finds. What workers should know

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1065 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Roth 401(k) matches are 'surging,' report finds. What workers should know

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1065 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Many more workers can now or will soon be able to accept a 401(k) match as a Roth contribution — giving them a latest avenue to build a bucket of tax-free savings for retirement.
    • Historically, workers could only accept 401(k) match money from an employer as pretax, meaning they had to defer income taxes on those funds until they withdrew them in retirement.
    • Until a recent rule change, workers generally couldn't elect to receive a match as a Roth contribution.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Many more workers can now or will soon be able to accept a 401(k) match as a Roth contribution — giving them a latest avenue to build a bucket of tax-free savings for retirement.

    Historically, workers could only accept 401(k) match money from an employer as pretax, meaning they had to defer income taxes on those funds until they withdrew them in retirement.

    Until a recent rule change, workers generally couldn't elect to receive a match as a Roth contribution. With Roth savings, investors don't get an up-front tax break — they pay income tax on the funds now but can take out the contributions and growth tax-free in retirement.

    It has been revealed that A law known as Secure 2.0, which former President Joe Biden signed into law in 2022, gave employers the option to add a Roth match as a feature of their 401(k) prepares. If a proposal offers a Roth match, it's not automatic; workers must opt in.

    The number of employers that now let workers accept a 401(k) match or other employer contribution as Roth savings has "surged," according to a upcoming report from the Plan Sponsor Council of America, a trade group representing employers.

    It has been revealed that about 42% of surveyed businesses that sponsored a 401(k) initiative in 2025 have added or will add an option to accept employer contributions as Roth savings, according to an annual PSCA report published Nov. 10. That's more than double the share — about 20% — that did so in 2024, the report found.

    Another 11% are still considering the option, according to the report.

    The PSCA report is based on data from 753 employers that sponsor 401(k) intends of various sizes.

    It has been revealed that "My guess is we will continue to see [the share] increase," said Hattie Greenan, the group's research director. "Roth is becoming mainstream," she said.

    But just because employees have the Roth match option available to them doesn't mean it will be their best option.

    There are pros and cons to pretax and Roth savings, and the right choice can vary from person to person, financial advisors mentioned.

    "[Roth] is not a bad idea if you're not so worried about your taxes today," said Philip Chao, a certified financial planner and chief investment officer at Experiential Wealth, based in Cabin John, Maryland. "It's personal preference.".

    While there are ample benefits to saving at least some money as Roth funds in a 401(k), most investors opt against it.

    In fact, while almost all 401(k) prepares already allow workers to save part of their paychecks as a Roth contribution, only a quarter of workers actually do so, according to the PSCA report.

    "The list of cons may be short for Roth 401(k)s, but missing tax deferral is a big one," according to a May article written by Fidelity, a retirement proposal administrator. "When faced with a choice of paying more tax now or later, most people choose to pay later, hence the low participation rates for Roth 401(k)s.".

    Tax deferral has long been a "key driver" of retirement savings, Fidelity said.

    Industry observers note that saving on a pretax basis effectively increases a worker's take-home pay. It also reduces their adjusted gross income today, and may therefore positively impact the calculation of eligibility for child tax credits, financial aid for college or federal aid, according to Fidelity.

    A Fidelity example demonstrates the financial benefit of an up-front tax break: Let's say a saver with a $75,000 annual income in the 22% federal income tax bracket makes a $400 monthly 401(k) contribution. Making the full contribution as Roth would reduce their paycheck by $400. Making the contribution into a traditional — i.e., pretax — 401(k) would reduce their paycheck by just $312.

    For those who can stomach the up-front tax hit, Roth provides for powerful tax-planning opportunities in future years, according to financial advisors.

    Recent findings suggest that "Roth gives you a lot more flexibility at retirement," Chao mentioned. "But you have to be OK with paying years of tax on it first. It's never something for nothing. There's always a trade-off.".

    In a recent development, for example, the government doesn't require investors to withdraw a minimum amount from Roth accounts in retirement, as it does with pretax savings. These annual "required minimum distributions," or RMDs, generally start at age 73 for traditional 401(k)s and IRAs, among other accounts.

    It has been revealed that additionally, withdrawing money from Roth accounts in retirement can help limit taxes on Social Security benefits and reduce Medicare premiums, which are based on taxable income. Roth withdrawals don't count as taxable income.

    Retirees can also make strategic withdrawals from Roth accounts in certain years to avoid jumping into a higher federal or state income tax bracket, advisors said.

    "Once you pay the taxes [on a Roth contribution], the government is out of your hair," Chao said. "There's no amount you must draw out. It's your money; it's all tax-free when you take it out.".

    According to recent reports, for example, many investors must wait until at least age 59 1/2 to withdraw funds tax-free from a Roth 401(k) account. Additionally, due to a so-called five-year rule, investors must have had Roth 401(k) funds for at least five years to make a tax-free withdrawal.

    Because Roth employer matching contributions are included in the saver's income, investors should ensure they have enough tax withheld from their paycheck to cover the income tax, according to Fidelity.

    The ultimate goal for savers choosing whether to make Roth or pretax contributions is to pay income taxes when their tax rate is lowest, advisors mentioned.

    For example, Roth savings can work well for younger savers over the long term if they anticipate their incomes — and tax rates — will grow over time, said Andrew Bachman, director of tax and retirement income on Fidelity's financial solutions team.

    Similar logic applies to people who plan to move from a low-tax to a high-tax state in retirement, such as from Texas to California, he said.

    While it's impossible to know future tax rates, investors can hedge by splitting contributions between both types of accounts, advisors said.

    Similar to contributions, workers may be able to split a 401(k) match between pretax and Roth savings. However, workers will be constrained by what their employer does and doesn't allow, Chao said.

At an annualized dividend of $4.28 per share, XOM offers a yield of 2.53%.

    Impressed by the Q3 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Exxon stock and raised his price target to $193 from $180 to reflect higher downstream earnings, with the expectation of increased mid-cycle margins.

    Industry observers note that gabelman noted that the strength in Exxon's refining business continues to offset Middle East-related headwinds. He added that the company increased its ownership in LNG projects, which should reduce its Middle East concentration over time from 75% to 50% and lower the likelihood of diversification-focused mergers and acquisitions. Beyond LNG, Gabelman expects Exxon's growth in the 2030s to come from Guyana, Kashagan, Permian, and possibly Venezuela.

    It has been revealed that gabelman noted that Exxon announced a dividend hike of nearly 4% and plans to maintain buybacks at $20 billion for 2027. "The decision to maintain reduces the pro-cyclicality nature of the buyback," noted the analyst.

    Sources indicate that in reaction to the Q3 2026 results, CIBC analyst Robert Catellier reaffirmed a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $82. The analyst noted that Q3 results were essentially in line with expectations and reflected continued strength in execution across WMB's infrastructure portfolio.

    Catellier said that Williams' Q3 performance was driven by higher transmission, storage, and power generation revenues, as well as contributions from the Momentum Midstream acquisition.

    He noted that Williams maintained its full-year EBITDA guidance of $8.3 billion to $8.5 billion.     Industry News: Ukraine damages Putin’s prized Crimea bridge as Zelenskyy lauds ‘unprecedented operation’

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ukraine has damaged the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, delivering a symbolic blow to President Vladimir Putin as Kyiv reels from strikes on its own infrastructure.
    • Sergey Aksyonov, the Russia-installed governor of Crimea, confirmed that the strategically notable bridge, which had been briefly closed on Monday, was attacked overnight for the second time in two days.
    • Videos and photos circulating on social media appeared to show the partial destruction of the bridge, with one section having collapsed into the water.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ukraine has damaged the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, delivering a symbolic blow to President Vladimir Putin as Kyiv reels from strikes on its own infrastructure.

    Sergey Aksyonov, the Russia-installed governor of Crimea, confirmed that the strategically notable bridge, which had been briefly closed on Monday, was attacked overnight for the second time in two days.

    Videos and photos circulating on social media appeared to show the partial destruction of the bridge, with one section having collapsed into the water. CNBC was unable to independently verify the footage.

    Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the attack as an "unprecedented operation" several weeks in the making, with Ukraine's defense forces, security services and weapons manufacturers involved.

    "Russia strikes our infrastructure every day, including bridges in Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Kyiv, and the Odesa region," Zelenskyy noted Tuesday on X.

    It has been revealed that "We are restoring our infrastructure. But we are also reminding Russia that war will always return to where it began. Ukraine's defensive capabilities are strong and will remain so, and we will never leave terror against our cities and people unanswered," he added.

    In a recent development, train and vehicle traffic was suspended due to the attack. No injuries have been reported.

    Ukraine has repeatedly targeted the bridge since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in early 2022.

    It has been revealed that A 12-mile crossing of road and railways, the Kerch Bridge is one of Putin's signature projects. The crossing, sometimes referred to as the Crimean bridge, was built on his orders shortly after the Kremlin forcibly annexed Crimea in 2014 to support Moscow's claims to the territory.

    Rail traffic on the bridge was opened on one track, Russia's Ministry of Transport mentioned in a statement via Telegram on Tuesday, while restoration work continues on the second section.

    The co-owner and chief engineer of Ukrainian missile and drone maker Fire Point, Denys Shtilierman, appeared to confirm the company's role in the attack, following reports that a Ukrainian Flamingo cruise missile was used in the strike.

    "We dedicate this to the memory of our friends and colleagues Andriy and Yuriy, without whom this would not have been possible. R.I.P.," Shtilierman remarked via X on Tuesday. A spokesperson at Fire Point separately confirmed the manufacturer's role in the attack.

    Analysts at the Institute for the Study of War, a Washington-based think tank, remarked Ukraine's attacks on the Kerch Bridge were likely part of Kyiv's ongoing and systematic strike campaign aimed at denying Russian forces the use of major ground lines of communication via Crimea.

    Russian forces, meanwhile, struck two bridges crossing the Dnipro River in Kyiv.

    Vitaliy Klitschko, the mayor of Ukraine's capital, noted via Telegram on Tuesday that specialists were working to assess the extent of the damage to the North and South bridges.

    Klitschko remarked Russian attacks on Kyiv overnight had also caused disruptions to water and heating supplies.

    The strikes come ahead of Putin's trip to China this week for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, where a trilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping is planned on Thursday.

    Asked whether Ukraine's latest attacks might be connected to the upcoming trilateral summit, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said this could not be ruled out.

    Sources indicate that "Combat operations continue, and our military is striking targets that are somehow connected to Ukraine's military-industrial complex. And Ukraine is continuing its terrorist attacks," Peskov mentioned, according to Russian state news outlet Ria Novosti.

    #15775. Tech Report: Deutsche Bank shares sink as whistleblowers reveal Epstein payments, Trump tax leak, Russia bets

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (497 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Deutsche Bank shares sink as whistleblowers reveal Epstein payments, Trump tax leak, Russia bets

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (497 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Deutsche Bank shares fell sharply in early trading on Tuesday after whistleblowers leaked about 15 million files from the German lender, with media reports revealing alleged historic failures across its risk management and financial crime controls.
    • These include suspicious payments linked to late financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and accidental leaks of President Donald Trump's tax statements.
    • The leaks contain board minutes, emails, internal investigations and other material that point to systemic failures across the Frankfurt-listed lender's business functions stretching back two decades.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Deutsche Bank shares fell sharply in early trading on Tuesday after whistleblowers leaked about 15 million files from the German lender, with media reports revealing alleged historic failures across its risk management and financial crime controls.

    These include suspicious payments linked to late financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and accidental leaks of President Donald Trump's tax statements.

    The leaks contain board minutes, emails, internal investigations and other material that point to systemic failures across the Frankfurt-listed lender's business functions stretching back two decades.

    In a recent development, shares in Deutsche Bank were 4.7% lower by 9:20 a.m. E.T., having fallen more than 6% in early trade in Frankfurt.

    Industry observers note that deutsche Bank processed $582 million in suspicious payments linked to Jeffrey Epstein, far more than previously known, the FT reported. Suspicious payments are not, by themselves, proof that every transaction was criminal.

    Sources indicate that the German lender also mistakenly leaked details of U.S. President Donald Trump's taxes in March 2017, during his first term in office, the FT said. The blunder — described by CEO Christian Sewing, who was then Deutsche's private banking head, as "an awful mistake" — was kept secret from the White House.

    The wide-ranging investigation — which was led by a consortium of more than 200 journalists worldwide including the FT, Der Spiegel and Le Monde — also stated Deutsche Bank had failed to offboard around 28,000 problematic investment bank clients who had been identified for removal by early 2018.

    It also alleges that the bank concealed information around cost targets in 2021, when external monitors in Latest York reportedly warned that Deutsche's risk appetite was running ahead of controls.

    According to recent reports, the files also contain details of the bank's relationships with oligarchs and transactions that the investigation links to Russian money-laundering concerns. It was these ties that motivated whistleblowers to send the information to Indian journalist Josy Joseph and South African journalist Khadija Sharife.

    The reports once again put Deutsche Bank's risk management practices and controls under the spotlight following years of regulatory scrutiny.

    The bank — which has been raided multiple times by German officials this year — has, since 2012, paid out some 18.6 billion euros ($20.5 billion) in settlements over alleged market manipulation, money laundering, mis-selling and misrepresentation, among other things, the FT said.

    In a statement, Deutsche Bank stated the issues detailed in Tuesday's media reports go back many years.

    "Where relevant, we reviewed these matters at the time and worked closely with regulators," the lender said.

    The bank stated it has undergone a "fundamental transformation" under CEO Christian Sewing, pointing to 7 billion euros of investment in its risk controls between 2019 and 2025.

    "Deutsche Bank is a different bank today and remains focused on executing its strategy which has proven successful, as evidenced by record profits in 2025 as well as in recent quarters.".

    CNBC has reached out to BaFin, Germany's financial regulator, for comment.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: South Korea will suspend all aircraft operation for 35 minutes and markets will open late. Here’s why

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (321 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • South Korea will suspend all aircraft takeoffs and landings nationwide for 35 minutes on Thursday to minimize noise during the English listening portion of the country's highly competitive college entrance exam, the government mentioned Tuesday.
    • It has been revealed that the restrictions will be in place from 1:05 p.m.
    • Planes already in the air will be required to remain at least 3 kilometers above the ground during the exam, while emergency flights will be exempt from the restrictions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    South Korea will suspend all aircraft takeoffs and landings nationwide for 35 minutes on Thursday to minimize noise during the English listening portion of the country's highly competitive college entrance exam, the government mentioned Tuesday.

    It has been revealed that the restrictions will be in place from 1:05 p.m. to 1:40 p.m. local time, affecting 130 flights, including 81 international and 49 domestic services, according to the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

    Planes already in the air will be required to remain at least 3 kilometers above the ground during the exam, while emergency flights will be exempt from the restrictions.

    Recent findings suggest that the measures will also apply to helicopters, light aircraft and drones, with all drone flights prohibited nationwide during the 35 minutes. Violators could face criminal penalties, the ministry stated.

    The government will adjust the departure and arrival times of affected flights, while airlines will notify passengers of the revised schedules in advance.

    The Korea Transportation Safety Authority will also send text messages to licensed drone operators, including those who have already received flight approvals, warning that drone flights will be prohibited during period regardless of prior authorization.

    "We will thoroughly implement the necessary measures, including restrictions on aircraft operations, to ensure students can concentrate ton the English listening test in a table environment," mentioned Jeong Chae-gyo, director general of aviation policy at the ministry.

    Jeong also urged airlines and relevant authorities to cooperate in adjusting flight schedules and notifying passengers in advance, and to advise travelers to check their revised departure and arrival times with their airlines.

    South Korea's college entrance exam, known as Suneung, is a high stakes annual test that plays a major role in determining students' university admissions.

    The country's stock market will also open an hour later than usual on Thursday, at 10 a.m. local time, and close at 4:30 pm, as revealed by the Korea Exchange.

    #15764. Demis Hassabis’ AI manufacturer raises $5 billion, months after he left as Google DeepMind CEO

    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Demis Hassabis’ AI manufacturer raises $5 billion, months after he left as Google DeepMind CEO

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (288 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Isomorphic Labs, an artificial intelligence drug discovery startup founded by former Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis, has raised a $5 billion Series C, the manufacturer stated on Tuesday.
    • Isomorphic's round comes three-and-a-half months after Hassabis stepped back as CEO of DeepMind, Google's AI lab, which he co-founded before the Significant Tech giant acquired it in 2014.
    • In a recent development, the round was co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, alongside Andreessen Horowitz, with investment from Alphabet, Google's parent.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Isomorphic Labs, an artificial intelligence drug discovery startup founded by former Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis, has raised a $5 billion Series C, the manufacturer stated on Tuesday.

    Isomorphic's round comes three-and-a-half months after Hassabis stepped back as CEO of DeepMind, Google's AI lab, which he co-founded before the Significant Tech giant acquired it in 2014.

    In a recent development, the round was co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, alongside Andreessen Horowitz, with investment from Alphabet, Google's parent. The fresh funds will help fund the design and development of latest medicines using AI.

    Drug discovery startups have seen record funding poured into them by investors in 2026 as companies look to capitalize on advances in AI. OpenAI and Anthropic have also been investing in tools to develop new medicines using the technology.

    Hassabis has been CEO of Isomorphic Labs since the startup spun out of DeepMind in 2021.

    "When we founded Isomorphic, our conviction was that biology could be understood and modelled at the most fundamental molecular level and radically accelerated through AI," said Hassabis.

    "This round enables us to accelerate our progress: building foundational biology models, deepening our systemic disease understanding, and driving our first therapeutic programs towards clinical trials to deliver tangible impact for patients," he added.

    Isomorphic is building a proprietary drug design engine and therapeutic candidate pipeline designed with AI, which it states will help it deliver the next generation of medicines.

    Anthropic announced it was launching an AI drug discovery program in June and OpenAI partnered with Novo Nordisk in April.

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (448 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
    • Sources indicate that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively fresh corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
    • The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    Sources indicate that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively fresh corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Industry observers note that securitize reinforced "certain areas of the firm like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    It has been revealed that securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The manufacturer posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Sources indicate that also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and revealed the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    • Michael Carrick remarked he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Michael Carrick remarked he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

    Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

    The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

    But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

    Recent findings suggest that “He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

    “We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”.

    Post-match video footage indicated Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

    Recent findings suggest that michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl.

    United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

    Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

    United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

    United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

    “It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”.

    It has been revealed that “It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a major season ahead.”.

    “It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”.

    Industry observers note that “We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have significant season and hope to win a trophy.”.

    Industry observers note that all over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

    Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

    Industry observers note that fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

    According to recent reports, two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right.     “Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”.

    “It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”.

    Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

    Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how newly introduced signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

    It has been revealed that one of those upcoming signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

    Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

    Sources indicate that cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

    This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

    “I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager remarked. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

    Industry observers note that “The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s manufacturer.     Investors look to Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's IPO to refresh the tech rally

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I've spent the past 20 years pushing back against the periodically popular notion that markets are replaying the late-1990s and early-2000s tech bubble and bust.
    • We've simply never matched the levels of gross overvaluation, pervasive public greed, fevered IPO issuance, corporate malinvestment and Wall Street malfeasance that set up a generational market peak, a halving of the S&P 500 over two-and-a-half years and a lost decade for stocks.
    • In a recent development, we still haven't.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I've spent the past 20 years pushing back against the periodically popular notion that markets are replaying the late-1990s and early-2000s tech bubble and bust.

    We've simply never matched the levels of gross overvaluation, pervasive public greed, fevered IPO issuance, corporate malinvestment and Wall Street malfeasance that set up a generational market peak, a halving of the S&P 500 over two-and-a-half years and a lost decade for stocks.

    In a recent development, we still haven't. Even if June was the peak in AI speculative fervor, as seems possible, and if Oct. 6 proves to have been a consequential broad-market top, the major indexes simply never stretched far enough into the thin air to make a potential retrenchment nearly as damaging as the early 2000s were.

    Still, in a more muted fashion, markets have been behaving in ways that generate uncomfortable comparisons to past buying climaxes accompanying a technology revolution.

    Sources indicate that there is still room and time for the market to prove that the messy sell-down in AI-reliant growth stocks is simply a painful adjustment phase and the S&P 500's six-month purgatorial range a mid-cycle refresh. But it will need to start getting on with it.

    Everyone wants to celebrate the way the market has absorbed the damage to semiconductors and other AI-buildout plays, rendering it a controlled demolition rather than indiscriminate destruction.

    The Financial Times Unhedged newsletter on Monday called it "The perfect sell-off," the same day the Wall Street Journal cheered, "When Nvidia Stumbled, Equal-Weight Funds Delivered.".

    Recent findings suggest that this is true, as far as it goes. A rush into defensive and "quality" stocks has largely offset the drag from Nvidia's $2 trillion market-cap loss from its October peak.

    But recent defensive leadership, especially from low-growth consumer staples and Massive Pharma, sends a less-reassuring macro message, and those groups lack the earnings momentum, narrative appeal or market-cap heft to carry a bull market to new heights.

    It has been revealed that BTIG technical strategist Jonathan Krinsky has noted echoes of the 2000 period when "boring" defensive stocks ripped as tech rolled over, supporting the tape for a while. Barclays equity desk noted Monday that the "quality factor" basket of stocks just had one of the best 100-day runs ever of the past 20 years.

    According to recent reports, and JP Morgan here plots the stampede into "low-volatility" stocks, mirroring the hasty retreat from "high-momentum" areas. There's room here for defensives to get even more popular before tripping multi-year extremes, but is that what an index investor should root for?

    As for the ascendance of everyone's favorite, the equal-weighted S&P 500, Ned Davis Research analyst London Stockton this month noted that just over 50% of S&P 500 stocks were outperforming the index itself in 2026. Sounds healthy, right? Only to a point.

    He explains: "Levels [of stocks outperforming the index] above 58% have most often occurred in and around years where there has been a large bear market." The current phase follows a period when leadership was extremely narrow, producing a "resemblance of the prior three years (2023-2025) to the two years prior to the last Tech bubble (1998-1999) with a very small percentage of companies outperforming the overall S&P 500.

    "It is not likely that we are in a situation like in 2000," Stockton concludes, "but this highlights the importance that these large tech stocks at the very least do not decline substantially for the S&P 500 to continue rallying higher.".

    Industry observers note that there are other straws in the wind that harken to prior tech busts:  The Federal Reserve is trying to restrain the corporate sector from overheating in the latter part of a cycle, same as in 1999. Retail traders have maniacally bought the cascading decline in Nvidia shares the past week or so, invoking the voracious dip-buying made famous in the late-'90s which worked until it failed spectacularly. The market's refusal to pay up for sizzling earnings growth raises alarms about whether they are pulled forward, unsustainable or overstated; profits from 2000 were later revised down radically.

    And Nvidia's alleged breach of chip-export rules and the forced departure of CEO Jensen Huang are a reminder that major corporate scandals were a key feature of the Tech Bubble's prolonged reckoning, though nothing resembling the multiple accounting frauds of that era are implied here.

    Again, this is the kind of litany of worry and woe that gets recited each time a tech-propelled bull market breaks stride for a bit; more often than not a recovery follows to clear the gloom.

    According to recent reports, perhaps Nvidia's results on Tuesday clearing the way for the organization to restart stock buybacks and the final allocation of Anthropic's IPO shares will refresh the tech bid. With luck, the huge "hyperscaler" tech-platform stocks will move back to the fore as well-funded stewards of a more sober AI expansion.

    Maybe, after weeks of Wall Street insisting that hedge-fund tech-stock positioning is scraping multi-year lows, this will finally presage an upside pain trade.

    The vaunted seasonal, post-election tailwinds that the consensus was expecting to fill market's sails and lift the indexes from the floor of an enervating six-month trading range are running late. They need to arrive quite soon. Otherwise, the soggy tape - along with signs of ebbing liquidity reflected in Bitcoin weakness a strong dollar and jumpier equity volatility - will make those tech-bust echoes louder.

    In a recent development, john Kolovos of Macro Risk Advisors on the latest reading: "Despite pervasive bearish sentiment and the average stock trading near latest highs, our historical studies suggest the market remains vulnerable to disappointment. With defensive leadership still dominating, risk appetite weak, and financial conditions still tight, maintaining a short-term cautious/bearish stance still seems warranted.".

    -Twenty years ago this week, I wrote a cover story for Barron's that antagonized plenty of friends in the stock-trading profession by foretelling a future of fast, cheap electronic markets that has largely come to pass.

    Called "Death of the Floor," the piece detailed the regulatory, technological and behavioral shifts that were ushering in high-frequency, low-touch trading and pressuring the old exchange model.

    Reading it now, the conclusions seem utterly obvious and inevitable, though at the time there were still 2,500 NYSE floor brokers and specialists trying to remain in the middle of most trades.

    It has been revealed that "For the specialists who manage trading in individual stocks and for the floor brokers who depend on the in-person auction model, a tough challenge is becoming even tougher. To stay in the game, they must master cybertrading. For the small investor, this is almost entirely good news. Trading costs should continue to fall, while the likelihood of getting the best price should improve.".

    Happily, exchanges have adapted and evolved – to zero commissions, thousands of ETFs and microsecond executions - and we have a market that can handle multiples of the capital flow that was routine back then.

    If I have one regret about the piece, it's that my good friend and former colleague Bob Pisani thought the CNBC reporter skeleton illustrating the article was meant to depict him.

    I assured him, many times, that it was not.

    -Almost every business relies heavily on its most loyal repeat customers. But this skew seems extreme for online-betting companies.

    Recent findings suggest that A Bloomberg piece picked up here by Yahoo Finance reports that one-third of all sports bettors produces some 97% of revenue at digital sportsbooks. It says the 1% most active gamblers on average lost 78 cents of each dollar bet, twice the loss rate of the norm among all customers.

    One can view this as simply paying for entertainment (I "lose" 100 cents of every dollar I place on a movie ticket), but the social disapproval toward the industry seems to have grown.

    Add it to the swirl of complications surrounding the legal and de-facto decriminalized wagering industry.

    Perceived hostility of Congressional Democrats to prediction-markets venues taking sports bets in states that haven't explicitly approved sports gambling is seen as a plus for DraftKings and Flutter.

    Meantime, Robinhood has blurred the lines between investing and gambling by aggressively expanding into prediction markets. And on Monday it was reported that Kalshi has looked to combine investing and betting from the opposite direction, acquiring a brokerage firm in order to offer stock trading to its prediction-markets clientele.

    It has been revealed that adults should be free to behave unwisely with their money in search of a windfall. But brokers promoting the negative-sum game of wagering while professing to help the little guy accumulate long-term wealth sends a dissonant message.

    The ducks that were quacking loudly ahead of SpaceX's June IPO are much quieter in advance of Anthropic's planned debut this week.

    Here is the year-to-date performance of two ETFs that hold shares of recent fresh listings, Renaissance IPO and First Trust US Equity Opportunities, relative to the S&P 500.

    As of June 12, when SpaceX priced, these funds had gone vertical as the public worked itself into an anticipatory lather, the Renaissance fund running ahead of the S&P by some 20 percentage points in the prior six months.

    Since then, the IPO funds have deflated (both now have large positions in SpaceX, of course) and there's a bit more focus on whether Anthropic's target valuation is justified given the vast rethink of the AI-proliferation thesis.

    All else being equal, a more favorable setup now versus then for a market being asked to swallow a latest $1 trillion-plus ticker.

    #15750. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (758 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (758 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • According to recent reports, huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the firm.
    • According to recent reports, nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    According to recent reports, huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the firm. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    According to recent reports, nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the tech giant to fulfill all of its previously revealed commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider noted in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    According to recent reports, tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    In a recent development, on Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    Sources indicate that it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The firm had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Recent findings suggest that neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    CoreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, stated CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he stated.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    Recent findings suggest that "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he stated in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    Industry observers note that bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real concern is just how much money the firm will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    According to recent reports, "Major companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he mentioned. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    St. Louis Fed's Musalem says four more rate hikes may be needed in coming months

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (351 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem indicated Tuesday that the central bank may need as many as four rate hikes in coming months, offering one of the most hawkish views yet by a Fed policymaker about the steps needed to quell inflation.
    • During a speech delivered in Argentina, Musalem made the case that current policy is not significantly restricting economic activity.
    • "The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve 2% inflation in a timely manner," he mentioned.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem indicated Tuesday that the central bank may need as many as four rate hikes in coming months, offering one of the most hawkish views yet by a Fed policymaker about the steps needed to quell inflation.

    During a speech delivered in Argentina, Musalem made the case that current policy is not significantly restricting economic activity.

    "The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve 2% inflation in a timely manner," he mentioned.

    Musalem mentioned the real policy rate, which subtracts the inflation rate from the Fed's target rate, needs to be between 2%-2.5% by next spring, and estimated that the current rate is about a full point below that range. That position suggests the Fed may need to hike at each of the upcoming Fed meetings in December, January, March and April.

    Musalem does not get a vote on the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee over the period where he notes that the rate increases will be needed, though he does get to present views and provide input on the "dot plot" of individual members' expectations. He will next vote in 2028.

    To be sure, Musalem noted "an unlikely but still plausible scenario" in which no further hikes would be needed.

    "Falling energy prices and lower shipping costs, or an increase in potential output growth driven by higher productivity growth, might ease inflation pressures such that inflation moves toward target in 18 months," he remarked. Another possibility is that demand might decelerate as spending on artificial intelligence slows.

    However, he remarked the more likely scenario is that "persistent strong demand and ongoing supply pressures" combine to keep inflation above the Fed's 2% target, thus requiring further increases in the fed funds rate from its current range of 3.75%-4%.

    Sources indicate that "It would be preferable for a higher real policy rate to happen in a balanced way, driven both by lower inflation and a higher nominal policy rate," he said. "However, the nominal policy rate may need to do most of the work.".

    • (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).
    • Industry observers note that is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?
    • Industry observers note that first, let's remember how we got here.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

    Industry observers note that is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

    Industry observers note that first, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout promptly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

    The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

    Industry observers note that zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three important forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

    This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

    For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

    The following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

    Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

    The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

    Industry observers note that the major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

    That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

    One crucial clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

    Any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

    We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

    The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

    It has been revealed that from here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see new highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

    #15734. Industry News: U.S. agencies say they initiated investigation into Nvidia partner Megaspeed in 2024

    Industry News: U.S. agencies say they initiated investigation into Nvidia partner Megaspeed in 2024

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (583 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the U.S.
    • Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia, has been drawn into the fallout surrounding the leadership shake-up at chip giant Nvidia.
    • In a joint release, the departments outlined a timeline of their investigations into Megaspeed, saying the probes began in 2024 over potential export-control violations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the U.S. Commerce and Justice Department on Monday stateside said they had initiated an investigation into Singapore-based manufacturer Megaspeed in 2024 to "address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting.".

    Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia, has been drawn into the fallout surrounding the leadership shake-up at chip giant Nvidia.

    In a joint release, the departments outlined a timeline of their investigations into Megaspeed, saying the probes began in 2024 over potential export-control violations.

    In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list, after Commerce Department investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales to the manufacturer.

    Sources indicate that in the same month, U.S. officials and Singapore police conducted an in-person inspection of Megaspeed and interviewed Alice Huang, who was allegedly involved in a relationship with Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang.

    "Following this enforcement action, the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed," the statement mentioned.

    In a recent development, on Wednesday, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick also reposted the statement, adding, "The Department of Commerce works to protect the U.S. economy and our critical industries every day. We are very proud of the work of the Bureau of Industry and Security.".

    Sources indicate that in response to the statement, Chris McGuire, senior fellow for China and emerging technologies at the Council of Foreign Relations wrote on X, "Very, very strange statement tonight... about Megaspeed. The facts here just don't add up, and this does nothing to explain why Commerce did not cut Megaspeed off from chips."McGuire said that Megaspeed kept buying chips after Nvidia put them on their no-trade list, and asked if Nvidia also blacklisted Megaspeed's subsidaries Speedmatrix and PT Megaspeed International. "I would bet they did not! If they kept shipping to them after blacklisting Megaspeed, that would be very concerning," McGuire added.

    Sources indicate that the statement comes after Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs said the first time authorities there learned of U.S. interest in Megaspeed and Alice Huang was in June. Singapore had already been conducting its own independent investigation and said she was not investigated for espionage.

    The city-state barred Alice Huang from re-entering the country in February 2026 after authorities found that she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed.

    Alice Huang was reportedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather information on Jensen Huang. The Justice Department has not reached a conclusion on whether she was a Chinese spy.

    According to recent reports, jensen Huang resigned as CEO last week after revelations about multiple extramarital relationships, including with two Nvidia employees. The tech giant has appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO.

    Sources indicate that the agencies' statement also comes as Nvidia prepares to report its third-quarter results Tuesday afternoon U.S. time, with Kress set to lead her first earnings call.

    Earlier on Monday in the U.S., the Commerce Department moved to close a loophole that has allowed Chinese companies to access Nvidia's advanced computing power through data centers in third countries.

    According to recent reports, the interim final rule from the department's Bureau of Industry and Security is aimed at restricting remote access to advanced U.S. computing technology.

    It also comes amid growing scrutiny of Lutnick for not having done enough to prevent restricted Nvidia chips and computing capacity from reaching Chinese companies.

    — CNBC's Anniek Bao and Dan Mangan contributed to this report.

    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Lisa Cook lawyer signals Fed gov won't attend Trump committee's hearing

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook's attorney on Tuesday gave the strongest signal yet that his client will not attend a hearing at the White House with a "committee of inquiry" investigating mortgage fraud allegations against Cook.
    • The committee established last month by President Donald Trump, who has previously tried to remove Cook from the central bank's board, is pretextual and poses a threat to the Fed, attorney Abbe Lowell wrote in a letter to presidential counsel Will Scharf.
    • "Governor Cook has no legal obligation to participate in an unfair hearing — and indeed, has a duty to the Federal Reserve to decline to participate in any proceeding that would undermine the institution's unique status and independence," Lowell wrote in the letter, which is dated Monday and was made public Tuesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook's attorney on Tuesday gave the strongest signal yet that his client will not attend a hearing at the White House with a "committee of inquiry" investigating mortgage fraud allegations against Cook.

    The committee established last month by President Donald Trump, who has previously tried to remove Cook from the central bank's board, is pretextual and poses a threat to the Fed, attorney Abbe Lowell wrote in a letter to presidential counsel Will Scharf.

    "Governor Cook has no legal obligation to participate in an unfair hearing — and indeed, has a duty to the Federal Reserve to decline to participate in any proceeding that would undermine the institution's unique status and independence," Lowell wrote in the letter, which is dated Monday and was made public Tuesday.

    The latest correspondence came nearly two weeks after the White House committee delayed its proposed hearing with Cook to Dec. 14 from Nov. 5. Lowell said that any hearing with Cook could not take place until at least December because of conflicts with her Fed duties.

    While Lowell had raised strong concerns from the outset about the legitimacy of the committee, he initially said Cook "welcomes the opportunity to present the facts so she can clear her name.".

    But he has continued to cast doubts on the both the committee's purpose and its composition of three executive branch officials, including National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett.

    Sources indicate that lowell's tone sounded more hostile than ever in this week's letter, the first known to be sent by either party in the matter since the Republican Party's devastating losses in the midterm elections on Nov. 3.

    He accused Scharf and the committee of seeking "only to manufacture 'cause' for a predetermined removal outcome.".

    According to recent reports, lowell highlighted two top concerns. First, he asserted that Hassett "is not competent to serve on any factfinding committee" because his prior comments about Cook "demonstrate that he has prejudged the issue.".

    Second, Lowell called it "fundamentally unfair" that the committee is demanding Cook hand over documents "immediately," while pledging to provide the governor with its own records just seven days before the hearing.

    "Your and the Committee's failure to address these legitimate concerns, over multiple weeks of back-and-forth correspondence, reinforces my prior observation: President Trump's decision to fire Governor Cook has already been made," Lowell wrote.

    "Consequently, this Committee process appears to be a façade designed to obscure a predetermined decision to fire Governor Cook or to unreasonably manufacture a supposed 'adverse inference' if she does not participate in a process that does not comport with the requirements of a fair hearing," the lawyer wrote.

    Lowell told Scharf that Cook would still be prepared to appear for a hearing if the White House "implements fair procedures." But the "ultimatums" Scharf gave in his last reply in early November "do not provide a productive path forward to enabling that participation," Lowell wrote.

    The White House did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on Lowell's letter.

    Trump, who frequently urges the Fed to lower interest rates, has long sought to fire Cook, an appointee of former President Joe Biden.

    It has been revealed that cook, the first Black woman to serve on the Fed's Board of Governors, last voted to cut rates in December 2025, siding with the majority. The Fed unanimously voted to raise rates after its most recent meeting in September.

    Trump officials sent a criminal referral last year alleging Cook may have committed mortgage fraud by falsely claiming different properties as her primary residence in order to get more favorable terms. Cook adamantly denied wrongdoing, and, after Trump tried to fire her in August 2025, filed a lawsuit to block her removal.

    According to recent reports, the Supreme Court in June prevented Trump from firing Cook, but gave him a path to try again if additional legal steps were taken. In August, the White House told Cook it was reviving its efforts to fire her on mortgage-related grounds. In October, Trump signed a presidential memo establishing the committee of inquiry to investigate allegations that Cook lied on records related to "one or more mortgage instruments.".
